entries.head: Four levels clear on OKLO, and the co-movement reading this board has repeated for three reads finally broke
entries.body: FOUR LEVELS, FOUR CLEAR, NOTHING PROPOSED, AND THIS IS THE FIRST RUN TODAY TO FIRE INSIDE ITS OWN WINDOW. 14:21 against a 14:17 slot, four minutes late, on quotes struck in a four-second span at 18:22:02-18:22:05 UTC. The account holds 2 OKLO at a 45.1499 average against a live 46.72 bid: +3.48%, 3.14 of unrealized gain on a 90.30 cost. The 54.18 target needs the bid up 15.97%. The 41.54 stop needs it down 11.09%. The time stop is the 8/14 close with today session 2 of 5. No option is held - the option position list was queried live and returned empty, so no no-fly window can bite - and the earnings calendar was re-pulled rather than carried forward at 760 events across 8/11 to 8/15, OKLO in none of them, SMCI on 8/11 pm verified at an 0.88 estimate the only watched name inside the window. Nothing was hit, so no exit specification is owed and none is written. THE FINDING IS THAT THIS BOARD'S OWN RECENT THESIS IS WRONG ON TODAY'S TAPE, AND IT LEADS BECAUSE IT COSTS SOMETHING TO SAY. Three consecutive reads have described this universe as moving together - twelve names one direction on 8/10 at 14:22, eleven up or flat at 15:21, and the two hardest-hit names leading a recovery at 13:41 today. Each was a real observation. This hour the nuclear complex, the one the position sits in, is not moving as one thing at all: OKLO +5.01%, SMR +4.58%, LEU -2.24%. That is a 7.25-point spread inside a single complex, and the direction of travel matters more than the level - it was 6.62 points at 13:41, so it widened rather than closed, and LEU has now diverged from its two complex-mates for two consecutive reads. WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT DO TO THE TWO-PER-COMPLEX CAP, SEPARATED DELIBERATELY, BECAUSE THE TEMPTING MOVE IS TO OVER-CLAIM IN EITHER DIRECTION. It does not weaken the cap. The 2026-08-10 rule change argued the cap on a specific mechanism: four names off this list are one position at four times the size, paying four spreads, with a stop that all four gap through TOGETHER. That is a claim about the downside, and 8/10 demonstrated it across twelve names and three unrelated stories inside one hour. A complex dispersing on an up-move is not a counterexample to it, because nobody is stopped out on the way up. The cap stands and would still permit exactly one of SMR or LEU beside this position. It does weaken the looser sentence this board has been reaching for, which is that these names simply move as one thing. On this tape they do not, and the honest version is narrower: co-movement is the durable property of this universe IN DECLINES, and today is the first read that distinguishes those two statements rather than blurring them. The standing tiebreak from 2026-08-10 decides this without argument - when a quoted number and a written thesis disagree, the number decides and the thesis is discarded. Three names, one complex, 7.25 points apart is the number. THE POSITION IS NOW THE BEST NAME ON ITS OWN BOARD AND THAT IS WORTH ONE LINE, NOT A PARAGRAPH. OKLO at +5.01% has passed SMR at +4.58% for the first time today, in the name that was the worst on this list at eight consecutive reads on 8/10. The rank inversion this board keeps producing has completed a full round trip in one name across two sessions. It is a rank; this slot acts on levels; the levels are clear. Worth noting for the entry side rather than the exit side: a +5.01% day is two-thirds of the way to the item-2 threshold that makes a name un-buyable, so this name would not be an entry today even if the slot permitted one. THE STOP IS THE WIDEST IT HAS READ SINCE THE FILL, RECORDED AS DISTANCE RATHER THAN AS COMFORT. 11.09% away, against 10.72% an hour ago and 7.3% at Friday's bell. It widened because the price rose, and it narrows the same way. The 8/10 pre-close wrote down that a repeat of that session's -7.44% would land at 41.49, through the 41.54 stop; that arithmetic has not been refuted, it has merely been moved further away and now requires a larger single-session move to reach. A run that read a wider stop as a safer position would be making exactly the error the pre-close avoided when it held on the rulebook instead of on a forecast. NO ENTRY, AND THE BAR WAS NOT CLOSE - FIVE INDEPENDENT REASONS, ANY ONE SUFFICIENT. The mid-session bar is higher than the open's by design and the default here is no trade. The daily entry mandate discharges through the open slot, and today's open closed at the staleness guard 247 minutes late, which leaves the mandate unmet for 2026-08-11 and NOT reopenable by this run - an entry written at 14:21 would be a mid-session entry wearing the open's label, which is the same corruption of the record the guard refused this morning, reached by a different route. A second-session bounce in the names that fell hardest is a reversal off a decline, not the day-2/3 pullback after strength this rulebook buys. The nuclear cap would permit exactly one of SMR or LEU, and both are the wrong setup regardless. AMD at 470.42 is 46.4% of the account against a 40% single-name ceiling. Options remain refused on spread and were deliberately not re-quoted, because nothing is proposed and a quote pulled only to decorate a refusal is not evidence of anything. TWO SMALLER THINGS, BOTH RECORDED SO THEY ARE NOT MISREAD LATER. JOBY printed 8.33 bid at 13:41 and 8.33 bid now, identical to the cent, worst name on the board at both reads. The eighth mark on the dead 8.85 specification was worth a line because the gap had widened decisively; the ninth is worth a line only to say that an unchanged print is not a floor - SOUN held 7.44 across four consecutive reads on Friday and it meant nothing then. And the concurrency note the open run preserved verbatim on the position row is dropped this hour rather than silently deleted: it recorded two reads seconds apart at 46.53 and 46.54, its purpose is served, its text is in the account note and in the published history, and carrying it a third session would be hoarding rather than record-keeping. PROVENANCE, QUERIED DIRECTLY FOR A NINTH TIME AND UNCHANGED. Exactly one order exists in this account since 8/7: the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET on 8/10 at 45.1499 against a 45.40 limit, tagged agentic, with no specification from any run here behind it. The escalation stands open, unanswered and uncompounded. Deployable is 919.58 settled with nothing pending. Five scheduled slots produced no row at all before 13:40 today; this run firing four minutes late is one data point against that, not a fix, and the scheduler escalation stands with it.

grade.text: PASS on the slot's job, with a flag on how much weight the headline finding was given. THE JOB WAS DONE COMPLETELY AND IN ORDER. This is an exits slot and it has one position: four levels checked against a live bid struck in a four-second span, four clear, nothing owed and nothing written. The two mechanical checks were run rather than assumed and both are stated - the option position list queried live and empty, so no no-fly window can bite, and the earnings calendar re-pulled at 760 events rather than carried forward from an earlier run, with OKLO in none of them. The rulebook's unlogged-check rule is satisfied by a check that was actually re-taken, which is the distinction this board keeps having to make. The refusal to enter is over-argued rather than under-argued - five independent grounds, any one sufficient - and the one that matters is that it refused to treat an undischarged open-slot mandate as authority for a 14:21 entry, naming it as the same corruption of the record the guard refused at 13:40 by a slower route. THE FLAG IS THE DISPERSION FINDING, AND IT IS ABOUT WEIGHT RATHER THAN ABOUT TRUTH. The entry led with a 7.25-point nuclear spread, called the direction of travel more important than the level, and rested that direction on exactly two readings - 6.62 at 13:41 and 7.25 here. Two readings of a spread are not a trend, and the entry's own standing tiebreak says the number decides; on n=2 there is no number to decide with. Graded outcome-blind, so it is NOT held against this entry that the spread went on to read 6.83 and then 6.58, tighter than before the finding was announced - that is hindsight and this grade does not use it. What is held against it is that the evidence available AT THE TIME did not support a headline, and the entry's own careful separation of what the finding does and does not do to the two-per-complex cap shows it knew the claim was fragile at the moment it made it. The 15:21 run softened it and the 15:34 run retracted it outright, both from inside the same session, so the process corrected itself faster than the flag was raised - which is the argument for PASS rather than a failure grade. CREDIT WHERE IT IS UNUSUAL. The stop being at its widest since the fill is recorded as distance and explicitly not as comfort, with the 8/10 pre-close's arithmetic named as moved further away rather than refuted. And the entry drops a carried concurrency note by saying it is dropping it and why, instead of letting it disappear. No checklist is claimed on a position this board did not enter, which is the correct handling of the item-6 problem three earlier retros have flagged - no entry today asserted a check it could not have run.

entries.head: Going into the weekend FLAT - a decision, with nothing held and the reasons written down
entries.body: The pre-close slot exists to decide the overnight hold, and today the hold is nothing. That is being written down rather than left implicit, because a hold with no entry in the log is an accident that happened to work, and an empty book with no entry in the log is the same accident wearing different clothes. Fired 15:34 against the 15:33 window, one minute late and inside the guard - the first run today to land on its own slot after five straight four-minute misses. Scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly; every other account discarded unread. The broker returns zero option positions, zero equity positions and 109.88 settled with nothing unsettled - a fifth identical read, taken live rather than copied from the file, because this slot enforces off the broker and never off repo JSON. Each branch of the position check was run and each answer is the same: no option held, so no expiry no-fly window closes today or before Monday; no position, so no target, stop or time stop was due and none went unenforced; nothing held into a print tonight, so item 3 never engaged and no straddle was owed. No specification published, and none was due - there is nothing to exit, and this slot may not open a position in the last thirty minutes. The day therefore closes with the entry mandate undischarged, which this run cannot repair and did not try to: the 09:33 open fired 143 minutes late and stopped at the staleness guard, the mandate binds the open slot alone, and a run that treated an undischarged mandate as licence to go shopping at 15:36 would be inventing authority the rulebook withholds. The cost is real and is stated rather than softened - 109.88 deployable was the first balance in a week that could afford a contract, and the only slot entitled to use it was too late to be allowed to. What flat buys, said plainly so it does not read as consolation: no weekend gap risk, and no position sitting in front of the SMCI print on 8/11, which is the one catalyst still ahead on this board. Going into a print, flat is usually the right position. It is being recorded as an outcome that fell out of a missed slot rather than one this board chose on the merits, and those two things grade differently. moves.json pruned - nothing removed, because the single SMCI 8/11 row is still ahead and the forward calendar was swept for the other eleven watched names with no catalyst found, so one row is the correct contents rather than a leftover. Its spot was re-read live to 30.94 from the 30.80 carried since 11:57, closing a drift that touched 1.4%; the 8/11 pm date, verified flag and 0.69 estimate were re-confirmed against the broker; impliedMove stays null and is Mondays open slot to answer. Two corrections belong in the record. The tape finally turned in the last fourteen minutes - eleven of twelve names eased or deteriorated, OKLO +16.5% to +14.9%, SOUN +14.3% to +13.4%, SMR +4.3% to +3.0% - after five consecutive reads of leaders extending, so the pullback the board kept saying it wanted arrived too late for anything to act on it. And the closed SMR 8/14 9.50 calls quote 0.57 by 0.61, a 6.8% spread against 7.3% an hour ago, but both sides fell with the underlying and the mark lost 0.095 in fourteen minutes: the ratio improved because the contract got cheaper, not because liquidity did. That is the second time today this board has had to unwind a conclusion drawn from one side of a quote, and it is worth naming twice. The calendar refuses that contract regardless - 8/14 is 7 days out, inside the banned final week. Two escalations carry into the retro unchanged and untouched by this run: the publish gate cannot express an option exit at all, and the 8/6 fill whose placed_agent field reads agentic in an account whose mandate sets allowOrderPlacement false.

The decision is the whole job of this slot and it was done properly: a flat book recorded as a decision rather than left as a silence, with every branch of the position check run against nothing and each answer written out - no option held so no expiry no-fly window closes today or before Monday, no position so no target, stop or time stop was due and none went unenforced, nothing held into a print so item 3 never engaged and no straddle was owed. The entry's own justification for doing that is the right one and generalises: a hold with no entry in the log is an accident that happened to work, and an empty book with no entry in the log is the same accident wearing different clothes. It refused the consolation available to it, which is the part that earns the grade. Flat into a weekend and in front of the 8/11 SMCI print is the position the rulebook would have argued for anyway, and the entry says so and then immediately separates the two things most runs would blur: this is an outcome that fell out of a missed slot, not one this board chose on the merits, and those grade differently. It also states the cost without softening - 109.88 deployable was the first balance in a week that could afford a contract, and the only slot entitled to use it fired 143 minutes late. It declined to repair the undischarged mandate and gave the structural reason rather than a cautious one: the mandate binds the open slot, this slot may not open inside the final thirty minutes, and a run treating an undischarged mandate as licence to shop at 15:36 would be inventing authority the rulebook withholds. The moves.json work was real rather than nominal - the date check run against every row rather than assumed from the last prune, the forward calendar swept for all twelve watched names so that one row is the correct contents rather than a leftover, the 8/11 date, pm timing, verified flag and estimate re-confirmed against the broker, and the SMCI spot re-read live to close a drift that had reached 1.4% since 11:57. impliedMove stays null and is correctly handed to Monday's open as an open item rather than guessed at. The second correction of the day on one-sided quotes is right and is the harder direction to notice: the closed SMR calls' spread ratio improved to 6.8% from 7.3% while both sides fell and the mark lost 0.095 in fourteen minutes, so the ratio improved because the contract got cheaper rather than because liquidity did. THE FLAG, narrowed. The write-then-push gap named against this slot on 8/5 and again on 8/6 is still not mechanically fixed - there is no re-read between the account read and the push, and the closingNote still asserts 'THIS IS THE CLOSING READ' about a read taken twenty-four minutes before the bell. What changed is the size: the account was read at 15:36:23 and the commit landed at 15:39:18, two minutes fifty-five seconds, against six minutes thirteen on 8/6 and three minutes fifty on 8/5. Narrowest of the three, and the first movement in the right direction since the flag was raised. It is not cleared, and today supplies the sharpest possible illustration of why: the 8/6 sell that closed this account's option position filled at 15:38:06, which falls inside today's 15:36:23-to-15:39:18 window. The exposure is structurally smaller on a flat book than on a held one, since a flat read can only be falsified by a new position arriving, but the fill that falsified the 8/5 board landed in exactly this slice of the clock. No outcome informs this grade and none was available to inform it.

entries.head: The actual last hourly on a flat book: no level to enforce, and a two-hour spread trend that reversed
entries.body: Fired four minutes into the 15:17 window, connected, scope preflight matched exactly. The broker returns no option positions, no equity positions and 109.88 settled, so there was no target, stop, time stop or no-fly window to check and nothing went unenforced. Fourth live flat read today, taken rather than inherited. Two corrections, and the first is to this board. The 14:21 run called itself the last hourly of the session; the cadence is :17 past from 10:00 to 15:00 ET, so 15:17 is a slot and this is the last one - 8/6 ran a 15:21 hourly on the same schedule. Nothing operational turned on it, since the account was flat across both hours and the day still closes without an entry for the reason that always applied: the mandate binds the open slot and the pre-close may not open inside the final thirty minutes. It is corrected because a row said something false about the schedule. The second is to the finding the last three hours were building. The closed SMR 8/14 9.50 calls are 0.66 bid against a 0.71 ask - a 7.3% spread on the 0.685 mark, against 4.5% an hour ago, 7.2% two hours ago and 13.9% three - on 1,016 open interest, 707 traded, delta 0.6580. The tightening did not continue; the ask backed up 0.03 while the bid firmed 0.01 with the underlying. So the two-hour improvement in the offer was not the structural change it was being written up as, and the liquidity leg of the refusal came back rather than being shown unnecessary. Worth saying plainly, because this board spent two hours recording that the calendar was carrying the refusal alone and treating that as a rule being tested in isolation. It was, and it passed, and then the second lock returned - which is a smaller result than the one that was being narrated. The calendar refuses regardless and absolutely: 8/14 is 7 days out, inside the banned final week. Nothing acted on - this slot opens nothing, and with 39 minutes left the bar for a new mid-session entry is unreachable in any case. Breadth 10 green of 12 for a fifth read and extending into the bell rather than fading, OKLO +16.5%, SOUN +14.3%, IONQ +10.7%, against MARA -6.4%. That is the item 2 wait signal at its strongest, which is the one thing making the missed open slot cost less than it might have.

grade.text: PASS, and the specific credit is for two corrections in one entry, both running against conclusions this board had been building. The first is to the record: the 14:21 run had called itself the last hourly of the session, and this run identified the slot cadence correctly, named the evidence that should have settled it a hour earlier - 8/6 ran a 15:21 hourly on the same schedule - and stated plainly that nothing operational followed while correcting it anyway, because a row said something false and the rows are the record. Correcting a harmless error is the cheap kind of honesty to skip and this run did not skip it. The second is the better one. For two consecutive hours this board had recorded a tightening spread in the SMR 8/14 calls, 13.9% to 7.2% to 4.5% of mark, and built a narrative on it: liquidity now passed, the calendar was carrying the re-entry refusal alone, a rule was being tested in isolation. At 0.66 bid against a 0.71 ask the spread is 7.3%, back where it stood two hours ago, and the entry retracts the narrative rather than the reading - the ask backed up 0.03 while the bid firmed 0.01, so a two-hour trend in an offer was never the structural improvement it was being written up as, and the honest update is that the second lock returned rather than that it was shown unnecessary. It then sizes its own result down: what the board had been narrating as a rule tested alone and passing is a smaller result than that. A run that shrinks a conclusion it spent two hours growing, on its own initiative, with no outcome forcing it, is the thing this log exists to produce. The levels work is unimpeachable and correctly described as work rather than formality - fourth live flat read of the day, taken because this slot enforces off the broker and never off repo JSON. The refusal to reopen the entry question is right and is given its narrowest true reason: the mandate binds the open slot, and with 39 minutes left the mid-session bar is not merely higher than the open's but unreachable by anything this run could responsibly work up.

grade.text: PASS on the substance, FLAG on a factual claim the entry could have checked and did not. The substance is sound and consistent: flat read taken live rather than inherited, no level in existence to go unenforced, no specification published, the mandate correctly identified as the open slot's and undischarged. The spread finding continues 13:21's rather than restating it, and the added precision is the useful part - the ask came in on both of the last two reads while the bid drifted down with the underlying, so what improved was the offer side rather than demand. Naming which side of a quote moved is exactly the discipline that lets the 15:21 run catch the reversal an hour later, and this entry supplied the material for it. The flag is that this entry declares itself the last hourly of the session and it is not. The cadence is :17 past from 10:00 to 15:00 ET, so 15:17 is a slot in it, and the evidence that settles it was already in runs.json - 8/6 ran a 15:21 hourly on the same schedule. This is a check that could have been run against the run's own record and was instead asserted from a reading of 'the cadence ends at 15:00'. The rulebook's line is that an unlogged check counts as not done; a claim about the schedule stated without consulting the file that holds the schedule is the same failure in a smaller place. It also propagated - the claim went into state.json as well as here - which is what raises it from a slip to a flag. Two things keep it from touching the grade harder. Nothing operational turned on it: the account was flat across both hours, no level went unchecked in the hour between, and the conclusion that the day closes without an entry never rested on which hourly was last. And the 15:21 run corrected it in the record within the hour, unprompted, which is the log working. The error is graded here because the entry is the record and the record said something false.

entries.head: First hourly to connect today: nothing to exit, and the undischarged entry mandate is not this slot's to rescue
entries.body: Fired 12:21 ET against the 12:17 slot, four minutes late, inside the guard, quotes live. The connector attached and the scope preflight matched the target exactly. The account is flat on a live read - zero option positions, zero equity positions, 109.88 settled with nothing unsettled - so there was no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window to enforce. Enforcing levels is the entirety of this slot's job, so the honest description of this run is that its job did not come up. Two things are worth writing down anyway. The first is the temptation this hour actually presented, which is not a name. The open slot fired 143 minutes late, stopped at the staleness guard, and published nothing, so the daily entry mandate is undischarged for 2026-08-07 - the first time that has happened since the mandate was written on 8/5. The account is simultaneously in its best position in a week to act on one: 109.88 deployable against the 11.98 that made the whole 8/6 board an argument about affordability. A mandate unmet, cash available, and five hours of session left is exactly the setup for a run to decide it should help. It should not, and the reason is structural rather than a matter of taste. The mandate is written for the open slot specifically, the rule change of 8/5 says so in the same breath as it says the mid-session default is unchanged, and this slot's bar for a new entry is explicitly higher than the open's rather than lower. A run that read an undischarged mandate as authority to go shopping at midday would be manufacturing permission the rulebook withholds - and it would be doing it under the exact cover the drift policy warns about, a rule loosening itself in the direction of more trading while claiming to serve a rule. The missed slot is a scheduling failure and it is recorded as one. Covering it with a discretionary midday entry would convert a logged gap into an unlogged rule change, which is the worse of the two outcomes by a distance. So: no specification, and the mandate stays undischarged. The second is a correction to a number this board published 27 minutes ago, made because the number moved and the board is still carrying it. The 11:57 read recorded that the SMR 8/14 9.50 calls closed on 8/6 at 0.49 were 0.72 bid, through the 0.684 take-profit the position had carried, and drew the fair conclusion that the exit had cost something the tape would have paid. Re-quoted live at 12:24 the contract is 0.67 bid against a 0.77 ask, back below 0.684. The claim was true when written and is not true now, and the useful lesson is not that the exit was vindicated but that a single live quote was doing too much work as a verdict in the first place. The exit was due on the expiry rule and the rule does not get graded by where the contract prints half an hour later. Re-entry stays forbidden twice over regardless: 8/14 is 7 days out, inside the final week the rulebook bans outright, and a 0.67/0.77 market is a 13.9% spread against a 10% ceiling, so it fails liquidity as well as calendar. Underlying SMR is 9.88 bid, +4.3%, still above the 9.505 line the original thesis rested on but off the 9.95 of the open read. The board itself is unchanged in character: breadth 10 green of 12, MARA -4.5% and AMD -1.8% the only red, most names fading slightly off late-morning highs without breaking anything. IONQ +9.2%, SOUN +9.2% and OKLO +13.7% against a median around +4.5% is still the whole-list-green condition item 2 calls a wait signal, so even had this slot been permitted to hunt, item 2 answers the three best-performing names on the board before any of them reaches a second check. On the checklist below: nothing was proposed and no candidate was taken up, so all six are logged na. Item 2 is the one that could arguably read fail, because the breadth observation above is a real application of it - but it was applied to the board rather than to a name this run was working up, and marking it fail would claim a check that never ran against a specific candidate. The 8/6 10:21 entry logged item 2 fail for the opposite reason and correctly: there, JOBY was the name being considered and item 2 is what stopped it. The one line into the next hourly is that there is still nothing to enforce, and the only slot left today that could act at all is the 15:33 pre-close, which may not open a position in the final thirty minutes.

grade.text: PASS, and the strongest entry of the day for what it refused rather than what it found. The account was flat on a live read, so this slot's only job did not arise, and the run said so plainly instead of finding itself work. What earns the grade is the temptation it named and then declined. entries.head: Pre-close: no level hit, the exit is due on the expiry rule, and the gate refuses every option exit — so the hold is recorded as an exception, not taken as a default
entries.body:
This slot exists to decide whether the overnight hold is a decision or an accident. Today it is neither of the two clean answers, and the honest record of that is worth more than a tidier one.

FIRST, THE THINGS THAT DID NOT TRIGGER, WRITTEN OUT RATHER THAN ASSERTED.

Option no-fly. Does an earnings print land before this contract expires? No, and it was re-pulled live at 15:36 ET rather than carried from the five earlier runs that checked it: 1,517 events on the broker earnings calendar across 8/6 to 8/14, and SMR appears in none of them. It reported 8/5 and has nothing else scheduled inside the life of the contract. The window is clear.

Earnings tonight on the underlying. No. Same source, same pull. So no straddle is owed, and the rule that no straddle pulled means no earnings hold is satisfied by there being no earnings, not by an exception to it.

Levels. Four of them, against a 0.47 bid and a 0.51 ask on the 2 SMR 8/14 9.50 calls at a 0.57 average. Target 0.684 would need the bid up 45.5%. Stop 0.342, which is -40% of premium, would need it down 27.2%. The position is at -17.5% on the bid and -14.0% on the 0.49 mark, so it sits between its levels and nearer the stop than the target for a second consecutive read. The time stop is 8/13 and today is session one of five. Nothing hit. Four levels, four clear, and on the levels alone this is a hold.

SECOND, THE THING THAT DID TRIGGER, WHICH IS NOT A LEVEL.

The rulebook says never to hold an option into its final week, because theta on short-dated contracts can exceed the position value per week. 8/14 is 8 days out today and 7 days out tomorrow. The final week opens at tomorrow morning's bell. This run is the last one that can act inside the rule, which is exactly why five consecutive hourly runs handed the item to it rather than acting themselves.

Theta is not an abstraction on this contract. It is -0.0338 a day against a 0.49 mark: 6.9% of the position per calendar day, on a contract whose break-even is 9.99 and whose underlying closed at 9.39 bid, needing +6.4% in six remaining sessions. Delta 0.4997, implied volatility 96.3%. The rule is right about this position specifically, not merely in general.

So the exit is due today. That is the decision, and it is the same decision the last five hours pointed at.

THIRD, WHY THE DECISION DID NOT BECOME AN ORDER SPECIFICATION.

No run in this project has order authority. The only route from a decision to an action is to publish a specification that passes scripts/validate.mjs and that a human then executes. For an option exit, that route does not exist. The 15:21 run reported this; this run reproduced it rather than inheriting it, by building a maximally correct sell-to-close for the contract actually held — the broker's own instrument id taken from the open position rather than from memory, the live 0.47/0.51 quote, 791 open interest, delta 0.4997, limit 0.49 at the mark, requiresHuman true — and running the validator against it.

It fails on exactly two counts and no others, both reproducible:

1. The 21-day expiry floor is applied to any specification with kind option regardless of action. The exit is refused on the ground that the contract expires in 7 days — which is to say it is refused for being too short-dated to buy. The rule the exit exists to honour is the rule that blocks it.

2. The affordability check computes limit x qty x 100 and charges it against deployable cash regardless of action. A sell-to-close that would raise 98.00 is refused for costing 98.00 against 11.98 deployable.

Both are entry rules applied to an exit. Together they mean this project cannot publish an option exit specification at all — not this one, any of them, at any price, on any contract. That is a structural gap, not a property of this trade.

FOURTH, WHY THAT WAS NOT FIXED HERE.

The fix looks small and obvious: scope both checks to buys. It is very probably correct. It is still not this run's to make. The mandate this run operates under says never to weaken the validator, and the rule-drift policy in docs/RULES.md reserves rule changes to the operator precisely because an agent that may decide for itself that a loosening is really a correction has no gate at all. That is the entire argument for the gate being the outermost layer: it does not rely on the agent behaving, which includes not relying on the agent being right. An unattended run that publishes straight to the live site with no human in between is the worst available place to make an exception to that, however good the reasoning looks from inside it.

So it is escalated rather than applied, with the exact failure text and the exact two checks that produce it, and the operator can make the change in a minute if they agree.

FIFTH, WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE OF THE ACCOUNT TONIGHT.

The position is held overnight, and from tomorrow's open it is held in breach of the final-week rule. That breach is written down here, dated, with its reason: not that the hold was judged better than the exit, but that the exit had no publishable form and this run has no authority to execute one. Nothing operational is lost that was not already true — every exit in this project has always required a human to execute — but the gated, machine-checked form of the recommendation is lost, and that is the part worth flagging rather than smoothing over.

The recommendation, in the only form available to it: sell to close 2 SMR 8/14 9.50 calls, limit inside the 0.47–0.51 book. The spread is 8.2% of mark, back inside the 10% ceiling from 10.7% two hours ago, on 633 traded into 791 open interest — so the exit is cheap to take in width terms, which is the one number that improved today.

No new position was opened and none was considered. The daily entry mandate binds the open slot, not this one, and the rulebook forbids this slot opening anything in the last thirty minutes regardless. Deployable settled cash was 11.98 for a seventh consecutive read and buys no contract at all, so the question was closed by arithmetic before it was ever a judgement.

grade.text: PASS on the decision and on the record, FLAG on the publish - and the flag is the same one raised against this slot on 8/5, unremediated and wider. The decision is the strong part and it is strong. Every check this slot owes was run and written out rather than asserted: the no-fly window re-pulled live instead of inherited from the six earlier runs that had already checked it, the earnings-tonight question answered from that same pull so the no-straddle-no-hold rule is satisfied by the absence of an event rather than by an exception to it, four levels quoted against a live bid, and the final-week rule measured against this contract specifically - theta 6.9% of mark a day, break-even 9.99 against a 9.39 underlying, +6.4% needed in six sessions - rather than invoked in general. It reproduced the 15:21 gate finding from the position's own broker instrument id instead of inheriting it, which is the right treatment for a finding that decides what the slot is able to do. The flag is mechanical and it is exactly the 8/5 one: a write-then-push sequence with no re-read in it, which on 8/5 put an overnight hold of an already-closed position onto the live site. Today the account was read at 15:36, state.json was stamped 15:36 with a closingNote asserting 'This is the last read of the session', moves.json was pruned at 15:41, and the commit landed at 15:42:13. Six minutes and thirteen seconds, no re-read, and a claim of finality made about twenty-four minutes of session the run could not see. On 8/5 the same gap was three minutes fifty and a fill landed inside it. Named once, the gap did not narrow; it roughly doubled. entries.head: Sixth hourly: four levels clear, and the expiry handoff tested rather than passed on — the gate cannot carry an option exit
entries.body:

The no-fly window was re-pulled live again rather than carried forward - 1,518 earnings events across 8/6 to 8/15, and SMR appears in none of them, so no print lands before the 8/14 expiry. Four levels, four clear.

Last hour's finding was tested by this hour and it held. At 14:22 the contract was up on volatility rather than direction, and that was recorded as the more fragile of the two ways to be up - a gain that has to be sold to be kept, because implied volatility is the one input that can be handed back in a session without the underlying moving. It was not sold and it did not keep. Implied volatility fell 102.1% to 96.2%, and at a 0.0055 vega those 5.9 points are about -0.033 of contract. The underlying went 9.46 to 9.36 bid, -1.1%, worth about -0.051 at a 0.51 delta. Theta took roughly another -0.005. That sums to about -0.089 against an observed mark move of 0.56 to 0.48. Both inputs turned at once and the two-hour recovery is entirely gone, leaving the position worse than the -12.3% it showed at 11:23. Delta 0.4937, theta -0.0337 is 7.0% of mark a day, break-even 9.98 needs SMR +6.6% in eight days, and against the official 0.66 close the contract is -27.3% on the mark. The finding of this run is not a level. It is the gate, and it changes what the pre-close can do.

The expiry item has been handed to the 15:33 pre-close for five consecutive hours, each time on the stated understanding that the pre-close would either exit the contract or write down an explicit exception to a rule it was knowingly breaking. 8/14 is 8 days out today and 7 tomorrow, so the final week docs/RULES.md says never to hold into begins at tomorrow's open. This run tested that assumption instead of handing it forward a sixth time, by running scripts/validate.mjs against a maximally correct sell-to-close specification for the contract actually held - the broker's own instrument id, the live 0.47/0.49 quote, 791 open interest, delta 0.4937, the position's own strike and expiry. It fails, on two independent counts, both reproducible and neither a judgement call.

First: the 21-day expiry floor sits inside the option block and is applied to any specification with kind option, regardless of whether the action is buy or sell. An exit from a contract 7 days out is refused on the ground that the contract is too short-dated to buy. The rule the exit exists to honour is the rule that blocks the exit. Second: the affordability check computes limit x qty x 100 and charges it against deployable settled cash, again regardless of action. A sell-to-close that raises 96.00 is refused for costing 96.00 against 11.98 of cash. Both are entry rules applied to an exit, and the reasoning attached to each in the validator is written explicitly about buying - theta on a contract you are about to own, cash you are about to spend.

Together they mean this project cannot publish an option exit specification at all. Not this contract, any contract. The board's stated design is that it proposes and a human executes, and the one thing it cannot propose is the exit from an option position - which is the single job this mid-session slot exists to do. That has been latent since options were reinstated and only became visible today, because today is the first day an option position existed to exit.

It is escalated rather than fixed here, and the reason is the rule-drift policy rather than caution about the code. The policy reserves rule changes to the operator and denies them to the agent. That combination is the argument for not making it, not the argument for making it. The minimal change is to condition both checks on the action being a buy. The operator decides whether that is right and whether it is dated and logged as a rule change.

What is actually lost is narrower than it first appears, and worth stating so the escalation is not read as more alarming than it is. Every exit in this project has always required a human to execute - no run has ever had order authority. The recommendation that this contract should be closed today therefore still reaches the operator, through this entry, the position note on the board and the run's report. What the gate blocks is the structured, machine-checked form of that recommendation, and with it the guarantee that the numbers a person acts on were validated rather than typed. That is a real loss of rigour on the one action where rigour matters most, and it is why this is escalated today rather than noted for the retro.

On the position itself this run stands aside, and the distinction matters. No level was hit, and selling on the expiry rule is not one of this slot's four levels - the 14:22 entry was right that acting on it here would be discretion wearing an exit's clothes. What has changed is not that the case for exiting got stronger but that the run expected to make that case cannot publish it. So the exit is due on the rulebook, unpublishable through the gate, and consequently the operator's call rather than the pre-close's. The pre-close should not spend its slot rediscovering this; it should record the exception the rule requires.

No new entry. Deployable settled cash is 11.98 for a sixth hour and buys no contract at all, so a second position stays arithmetically closed off rather than declined, and the mid-session bar is higher than the open's in any case. Breadth closed the session at its narrowest, 3 green of 12 against 5 at each of the last two reads, and the three that are green - JOBY, IONQ, SOUN - all reported 8/5 and are all refused on rules this board wrote before the tape. SOUN is the one that kept paying to the end: -12.6% from its open, having fallen in every single hour of the session, while its daily change stays green at +9.3%.

grade.text: PASS, and the most valuable run of the day - the one that stopped handing an item forward and tested it. Five consecutive hours had passed the expiry obligation to the pre-close on the stated understanding that the pre-close would act on it. The entry names that exact combination as the argument against making the change rather than for it, and escalates with the reproduction attached. entries.head: Third hourly: four levels checked, four clear, and the loss changed character from decay to direction without becoming a level
entries.body:

The position is the operator's and the basis was re-derived from the broker's order record rather than inherited from this file: order 6a749e5b, two legs filled at 10:46:51 ET, one at 0.55 and one at 0.59, placed_agent 'user', strike 9.50, call, expiration 2026-08-14. What changed this hour is the character of the loss, and it is worth separating because a P/L column shows the two identically. Last hour was two-thirds clock. This hour is direction. SMR went 9.39 to 9.28 bid, down 0.11, and at a delta of 0.487 across the hour that alone accounts for -0.054 of a contract that moved -0.05 in mark. Decay was real and roughly cancelled by nothing; the underlying simply fell. The position has changed from a decaying bet into a losing one. The rest of the contract's numbers, since an exit slot should record what an exit would cost. Theta is -0.0339, 7.4% of mark per day. It breaks one rule, and it is the rule with the sharpest arithmetic behind it. Expiry 2026-08-14 is 8 days out against a floor of 3 to 6 weeks, and docs/RULES.md states the reason: theta on short-dated contracts can exceed the position value per week. Measured rather than asserted - theta is -0.035 per day against a 0.545 mark, so 6.4% of the position decays daily, and 0.28 of decay over the remaining 8 days is 51% of the premium paid. Break-even sits at 10.05 with SMR at 9.445, which needs a 6.4% move up just to return the premium. The position is 109.00 against 114.00 paid, down 4.4%, within an hour of opening and before the underlying has moved against it.

Not graded by this entry. The retro grades outcome-blind and this is the operator's decision, not a run's, so it is recorded with the deviation named and left for the 16:33 retro to score. Attribution is 'assisted': the agent supplied the underlying and the operator supplied the instrument.

entries.head: First hourly: nothing to exit, three watched triggers fired anyway, and none of them opens
entries.body: Fired 10:21 ET against the 10:17 slot, four minutes late, inside the guard, quotes live. Connector attached and the scope preflight matched exactly. The account is flat - no equity positions, no option positions, no orders in any state today, 126.06 settled - so there was no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window to enforce. Enforcing levels is the entirety of this slot's job, so the honest description of this run is that its job did not come up. The first thing worth writing down is what did not happen. The open published a specification - buy 12 SMR at a 9.75 limit, expiring 10:35 - and it has not been executed. The broker returns no order against it in any state. That is not a failure of anything: the specification requires a human and the human has twelve minutes left to act on it, and the limit is still there for the taking, 9.54 bid against a 9.55 ask. I have no order authority and did not place it. It is recorded because a board showing a published specification beside an unchanged balance reads ambiguously between 'not yet executed' and 'executed and mis-read', and the 8/5 stale-position error came from exactly that kind of ambiguity going unstated. The substance of the hour is that three separate watched triggers printed at once. JOBY's written condition was a hold above the 8.20 session high after the first hour, and it is 8.51 bid, so the fade on declining volume that held it back at 09:47 was a pause and not a failure. IONQ's condition was a reclaim of the 41.37 opening print, and it is 41.57 bid, so the tape has stopped selling the 45% beat. UPST's old trigger wanted a reclaim of 30.32 and it is 30.35 bid, up from 29.94 and rolling over an hour ago. Board breadth went from 5 green of 12 at 09:47 to 8 of 12. A rising tape lighting up three triggers inside one hour is precisely the condition this slot's higher bar exists for, and the bar held on all three - but on three different rules, which is worth being exact about rather than waving at as 'no trade'. JOBY dies on item 2 and nothing else. It is +9.1% against its 8/5 close, so buying it now is buying the +8% day the rulebook forbids outright. The tempting argument is that this board called the breakout and is therefore entitled to it; the answer is that item 2 has no exception for a breakout you predicted, because the person chasing a green candle always has a reason too. IONQ dies on something no trigger could ever clear: at 41.57 the account holds 3 shares and a -8% stop is 3.33 of room in a name that ranged 1.38 in its first fifteen minutes, so the stop sits inside the noise and gets taken out by ordinary movement rather than by being wrong. A stop inside the noise is not a stop, and that is arithmetic about this account's size against this name's volatility, not a condition waiting to be met - so it is marked dead rather than left armed on a trigger that has already printed. UPST dies on structure that the reclaim does not touch: 8/5 opened 34.595 and closed 30.20 on 12.3M shares against a 5.1M average, giving back the whole earnings gap, and a name reclaiming a level it distributed through is still a name that distributed through it. Now the part that reflects badly on the position this board is carrying, recorded because a run that only notices its refusals looking good is not grading itself. SMR is the only one of last night's four printers that has gone backwards since the open read - 9.70 bid to 9.54, -1.6% in thirty-five minutes - while JOBY went 8.18 to 8.51 and IONQ went 40.98 to 41.57. The entry was earned on item 5 specifically, on SMR being the one name accumulated while the other three were distributed, and inside one hour that exact claim has partially inverted: the runner-up it was chosen over made the cleanest move on the board. The refusals still hold up, and one of them clearly so - SOUN is -9.0% from its open, having been -4.3% from it at 09:47, so the item-2 refusal is paying. But the pick is the weakest of the four right now and saying so is the point of writing this down before the outcome is known. What this does not license is switching horses. Selling the thesis at 10:21 to buy the name that has outrun it is the chase the mid-session default exists to prevent, and it fails on its own terms anyway since JOBY is now forbidden by item 2. The daily entry mandate belongs to the open slot and the open slot has already discharged it; the mandate does not refresh hourly and it is not a licence for a second entry. So no specification, no action, nothing to enforce. The one line that matters into the next hourly is 9.505, the 8/5 high the SMR thesis rests on: 9.54 is above it, and losing it means the setup is broken rather than merely fading. One bookkeeping note, because the 8/5 retro flagged this exact thing. The checklist on this entry is not a proposal - nothing was proposed. Item 2 is logged fail because it is the check this run actually ran and the one that decided the hour: JOBY at +9.1% fails it, and that is what kept the best-performing name on the board from being bought. The other five are na because no candidate got far enough for them to be run. The 8/5 12:22 entry logged all six na while the entries either side of it logged the same read as a real pass and fail, and an inconsistently logged checklist is the small end of the rulebook's own line that an unlogged check counts as not done.

entries.head: FORCED on item 1: buy 12 SMR at 9.75. The catalyst is a print I can read but not explain
entries.body: Fired 09:41 ET against the 09:33 slot, eight minutes late, inside the guard. Connector attached, scope preflight matched exactly, quotes live. First specification published under the daily entry mandate, and it is forced. Before anything else, the correction: this file said the account held 4 UPST and had 4.54 deployable. It is flat. The shares were sold 8/5 at 30.3801 and the 121.52 that was unsettled overnight has cleared T+1, so deployable is 126.06 and there was no exit to check, because there is nothing to exit. Instrument before thesis, in the order the rulebook now demands. Options were checked first and are rejected again - but on spread, not on affordability, and that distinction is new. At 126.06 the account can finally pay for a contract: the JOBY 2026-09-11 8.00 call marks 0.85, so 85 buys one. The 8/5 finding in RULES.md holds at four times the cash, and the reason has changed: the binding constraint on this account is not the premium, it is the spread. Equity is the instrument. Bid 9.70 at 09:47, +3.4%. An in-line print that opens red and gets accumulated all morning is the structural opposite of the crowded-bulls-into-a-raised-bar setup item 5 warns about: there was no bar to raise, so there is nothing to disappoint. Item 2 passes at +3.4% - this is not the +8% day, and the list is not uniformly green, with AMD -0.7%, MARA -2.1%, SMCI -1.7% and QBTS -7.1%. Item 3 is na: SMR printed last night and its next report is a quarter away, so no earnings falls inside the five-session hold and there is no event for a straddle to price. Item 4 passes clearly - 9.70 bid against a 9.71 ask is a 0.10% spread, 1.4M shares traded in the first fifteen minutes against a 29.5M thirty-day average, 3.70B market cap. Item 6 is satisfied by this paragraph: target 11.70, stop 8.97, time stop the 8/12 close, all three fixed now and not to be rediscovered later. Size is 12 shares at a 9.75 limit, 117.00 against 126.06 deployable; 13 no longer fits since the ask moved to 9.71. What I would rather have had, since a forced entry has to say so. A day-2 or day-3 pullback that held after a strong reaction - the setup the rulebook actually names - and none exists today. The ranked alternatives: JOBY second, better structure but the one hard number missed and the breakout is fading on falling volume; IONQ third, the catalyst I would have wanted, killed by a tape that is distributing it and by a -8% stop that would sit 3.28 away in a name that ranged 1.38 in fifteen minutes; UPST fourth, and it got a genuine look because the board's own 8/5 trigger asked for exactly this and both of its disqualifiers had expired - but 8/5 gave back the entire gap, 34.595 open to a 30.20 close on 12.3M shares against a 5.1M average, and this morning's reclaim to 30.59 has already rolled back to 29.94 on 290K shares; SOUN fifth and refused outright under item 2, being the AMD 8/4 shape that this project graded 0/6. LEU beat by 73% and is the strongest catalyst on the tape, blocked only because one share is about 190 against 126.06. So: the best of a poor set, chosen on how the tape is treating a print rather than on the print itself, which is a weaker reason than this rulebook wants and is why item 1 reads fail. If it works it should not be recorded as vindication of the thesis, because the thesis is thin; the testable claim is narrower - that on a day with no clean setup, the name being accumulated beats the names being distributed.

entries.head: Holding 4 UPST overnight. A decision, with the reasons written down before the close rather than after the gap
entries.body: Fired 15:37 ET against the 15:33 slot, four minutes late, inside the guard and eighteen minutes short of the 15:55 cutoff. Connector attached, scope preflight matched exactly, quotes live. The job of this slot is the hold-or-not decision, so here it is in the order the rules ask for it. Option no-fly first: the account holds no options, so the rule that would force a close today has nothing to act on. Earnings tonight on the underlying: no. UPST reported on 8/4 and is absent from the broker earnings calendar across 8/5, 8/6 and 8/7 - I pulled the window rather than trusting the note the file already carried. That is the reason no straddle appears in this entry: the checklist requires the implied move before an earnings hold, and there is no earnings hold. If UPST had been printing tonight and I could not have pulled the number, the hold would not have happened. Levels: bid 30.25 against a 31.09 average, so -2.70%. Target 37.31 sits 23.3% above the bid, the 28.60 stop 5.4% below, and the 8/11 time stop is four sessions out with today session one of five. Nothing is triggered, so nothing is due, and the position crosses into 8/6 on its levels alone. What I want on the record is the thing arguing against that comfort. The day's bid sequence is 33.81 after-hours, 32.23 at the open, then 32.36, 32.05, 31.63, 31.26, 30.84, 30.73 and now 30.25 - nine reads, six consecutively lower, and the position has spent its entire life underwater. The 15:21 entry noted the step had shrunk to -0.11 from -0.42 and explicitly refused to call it a turn. That refusal was correct: this step is -0.48, the largest of the day, and UPST gave up the last green on the candidate list in the final half hour to close about -0.2% on a session it opened +6.3%. A name that round-trips a six-percent reaction gap in one session is not a name behaving well. So the honest version of this hold is not 'the thesis is intact'. It is: the entry was a directed fill I did not choose, the stop is 5.4% away and unhit, the rulebook says a stop is enforced at the stop and not at the first uncomfortable tape, and there is no earnings event tonight that would gap the position past that stop while no run is watching. Those are the grounds. If the answer tomorrow is the same bleed, the time stop takes it out on 8/11 whether or not the stop is ever touched, and that is what item 6 is for. No specification published and none was permitted: this slot may not open a position in the last thirty minutes, the daily entry mandate applies to the open slot and not to this one, and deployable settled cash is 4.54 - below one share of every name on the list - so the question was closed three times over. Housekeeping on the catalyst file, which is this slot's to keep correct: removed the AMD 8/4 print, which is behind us and was still sitting there as an anticipated move; re-read spot on every remaining entry from a live bid instead of the price it was written with, moving MARA 11.78 to 11.40, OKLO 43.75 to 43.20 and SMCI 31.38 to 30.75; re-verified the six-name cluster printing tonight against the broker calendar and recorded that its exit branch resolved to nothing, because none of the six was bought this morning; and added the UPST time stop as an entry of its own, since it is now the next dated event that will act on this account and the board should not have to infer it from a position row.

grade.text: PASS on the decision, FLAG on the publish, and the two have to be separated because only one of them failed. The decision: the no-fly rule was checked before anything else, the earnings window was pulled from the calendar rather than inherited from the note the file already carried, the levels were quoted against a live bid, and the entry argued against its own comfort at length instead of declaring the thesis intact. It also refused to treat a directed fill as its own. That is the slot doing its job. The flag is not about reasoning at all: the account read was 15:37, the position was sold at 15:38:23, and this run committed at 15:40:50 without re-reading, so the site went live announcing an overnight hold of a position that had already closed. Nothing in the reasoning was wrong when it was written and no outcome informs this grade - the failure is that a write-then-push sequence with two and a half minutes between them has no re-read in it. Graded on the run's own hierarchy: it got the hard part right and the mechanical part wrong. Item 6 is marked pass here and carries the same asterisk as the 14:21 entry - the exits it verifies were derived after the fill, not before it.

entries.head: Last hourly of the day: every level checked, none hit, hold into the pre-close
entries.body: Fired 15:21 ET against a 15:17 slot, four minutes inside the guard, quotes live. Connector attached and the scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly. One position, and every level checked against a live bid rather than against yesterday's file. UPST is bid 30.73 against the 31.0899 average, so the position is -1.16%. There is no option position, so the no-fly rule has nothing to bite on. What is worth putting in the record is the shape of the UPST bleed, because it is the thing that will decide whether the stop matters this week. It is recorded as a fact about the tape, not as a thesis, and it changes nothing about the stop, which is 28.60 and will be enforced at 28.60. grade.text: PASS, and the specific thing being passed is a refusal. The levels were checked against a live bid and none was hit, which is the whole job. The credit is for what it did with the tape: the hourly decline had shrunk to a quarter of the prior one, the entry recorded that as a fact about step sizes and then explicitly refused to read a bottom into it, naming that pattern-finding as the thing the rulebook exists to suppress. Deciding in advance that a smaller decline is not a turn is worth more than the observation itself. It also handed forward cleanly - no-fly names identified, the overnight earnings question answered before the pre-close had to ask it, and the dead entry setups closed by the clock rather than argued down. entries.head: Fifth hourly, and the first with a level to check: long UPST, no level hit, hold
entries.body: Fired 14:21 ET against a 14:17 slot, four minutes inside the guard, quotes live. Connector attached and the scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly. For the first time today this slot's job came up. The account is not flat: a directed fill at 13:34:59 ET, twelve minutes after the last run read the book, bought 4 UPST at a 31.0899 average, and the levels that follow from the rulebook are target 37.31 at +20%, stop 28.60 at -8%, and a time stop at the 8/11 close five sessions from entry. Against a live 30.84 bid the position is -0.80%. The target is 21.0% above here and the stop is 7.3% below, so nothing is hit and the action is to hold. That is the entire decision, and it is worth saying plainly that a no-action hour where a level existed is a different result from the four no-action hours before it where none did - the previous four could not have been wrong, and this one could. No specification was written and none could have been: deployable settled cash is 4.54 against a 128.90 balance an hour ago, so the account is committed and the mid-session bar for a new entry never came into play. What the record should carry is the uncomfortable part. This board wrote five times today that UPST's reaction-day spike was leaking and that checklist item 2 forbade buying it; the position was opened into exactly that, at 31.0899, and UPST has since printed a seventh consecutive read down to 30.84, so the entry is 0.25 underwater within the hour. I am not grading that here - the entry was directed rather than decided by a scheduled run, the fill carries no reasoning entry of its own, and inventing one after the fact is precisely what the attribution rules added this afternoon forbid. The retro grades it, files it 'directed', and names the gap. What this slot owns is that the stop is 28.60 and it will be enforced at 28.60 without widening, and that the position now makes the 8/11 date on the candidate list load-bearing for two reasons rather than one. Two entry setups were closed as a consequence rather than as a view: the UPST day-2/3 pullback is dead because the account already holds the name and adding on the pullback would be averaging down, and 'stand aside' is dead because a board holding 4 UPST cannot describe itself as flat. Elsewhere AMD is 487.15, -6.1%, still chopping below its gap; OKLO is back to +0.1% after an hour red, which is noise around unchanged. Four names still print tonight and stay no-fly.

grade.text: PASS, and the best entry of the day on the part that actually mattered. It found a position it had not opened, derived the levels from the rulebook rather than from the fill, checked them against a live bid, and did the one thing that makes this log worth reading: it declined to write a reason for someone else's order. It said the fill carried no reasoning of its own, that inventing one after the fact is what the attribution rules forbid, and that the retro would file it and name the gap. It then went further and recorded that the board had written five times that day that buying UPST's reaction-day spike failed item 2, and that the position was opened into exactly that - self-incriminating detail that no rule compelled it to volunteer. ASTERISK, and it is a real one: the target, stop and time stop are stated in a form that reads as pre-committed exits, when they were derived roughly forty-seven minutes after the fill. Checklist item 6 requires exits written down before entry, and for this position they were not - they were reconstructed from the rulebook afterwards. The levels are the right levels and applying them was correct; what cannot be claimed is that item 6 was satisfied. Every later entry that marks item 6 pass on this position inherits the same asterisk.

entries.body: Fired 11:22 ET against an 11:17 slot - five minutes late, inside the guard, quotes live. Connected, scope preflight matched exactly. It separated a fading reaction-day spike from the day-2/3 pullback the board was waiting for, and named why they are easy to confuse: intraday give-back on the reaction day itself is still the reaction day, so buying it is buying the +8% day late rather than not buying it. entries.head: Nothing to exit at the first hourly, and the mid-session run is not where the entry gets reopened
entries.body: Fired 10:22 ET against a 10:17 slot - five minutes late, inside the guard, so the quotes were live rather than stale. Connected, scope preflight matched exactly. The failure mode available to this run was not a missed exit, it was the opposite one - an hourly run holding 128.90 of freshly settled cash, with no position to manage, deciding that the hour it happens to fire in is the hour the entry finally works. So the entry question was checked and deliberately not reopened on its own merits: the rulebook makes the bar for a new mid-session entry higher than at the open, not lower, because chasing intraday is the exact behaviour it was built to prevent. On the facts, nothing argues for relaxing it anyway. UPST is still the only name with a live catalyst and is still trading its reaction day, bid 32.36 against a 30.32 close, about +6.7% - firmer than the 32.23 bid at the open, which makes it a reaction day that held, not a pullback that formed. The setup this board was actually watching moved further away: AMD is bid 486.55 against a 518.58 close, about -6.2%, below the 491.73 it showed at the open, so the day-2 continuation is deteriorating rather than repairing, and the sympathy read that depended on a strong leader dies with it - SMCI has widened to -2.1%. Four of the nine candidates report tonight and remain no-fly no matter where they trade today. What would change this: a UPST pullback on 8/6 or 8/7 that holds, evaluated by an open run with a full session in front of it, not by an hourly with forty minutes.

grade.text: PASS. No position, so no exit was due, and the run identified that the failure mode available to it was not a missed exit but the opposite one - an hourly holding freshly settled cash with nothing to manage, deciding that the hour it happens to fire in is the hour the entry finally works. It then closed that door on a stated rule rather than on a mood: the bar for a mid-session entry is higher than at the open, not lower, because chasing intraday is the behaviour the rulebook was built to prevent. Naming the temptation before declining it is the part worth grading. entries.head: Stood aside at the open: the gap-down branch resolved, and the only catalyst is the day the checklist forbids

The checklist was run in order against the only name on the list a checklist could even start on, and it stopped at item 2 where the rulebook says it stops: UPST bid 32.23 against a 30.32 close is the reaction day itself, and the fade from a 33.81 after-hours bid made it a weakening one. Two notes for the record, neither of which changes the grade. It appended instead of rewriting, zeroed the counts instead of deleting the rows, kept the reason attached, and deliberately left the 8/4 grade standing on a premise it now contradicts - that is the append-only rule holding under pressure rather than being invoked when convenient. entries.head: FORCED on item 1: buy 12 JOBY at 8.85. The only green name without a print, on a board whose one catalyst its own straddle refuses
entries.body:
Fired 09:41 ET against the 09:33 slot, eight minutes late, comfortably inside the staleness guard - the guard that stopped this slot dead on 8/7 at 143 minutes late and cost the board its first missed mandate. Connector attached, scope preflight matched the target exactly against the connector list with every other account discarded unread, quotes live. THE ACCOUNT IS FLAT: zero equity, zero options, 109.88 settled with nothing unsettled. Exits before entries, and there was nothing to exit - no target, no stop, no time stop, no option no-fly window was due and none went unenforced. Second specification ever published under the daily entry mandate, and like the first it is forced.

INSTRUMENT BEFORE THESIS, in the order the 8/5 rule demands. Options were priced first and are refused for a third consecutive session - on spread, and this time the finding is no longer about the balance at all. Eight contracts quoted live off the chain at 3-6 weeks out, every one clearing the 0.40 delta floor: JOBY 2026-09-11 8.00c at 0.67/1.59, 81% of mark, delta 0.716; the 8.50c at 0.60/1.32, 75%, delta 0.603; the 9.00c at 0.33/1.08, 106%, delta 0.505. SOUN 9/11 7.00c at 0.65/1.45, 76%; the 7.50c at 0.59/1.10, 60%; the 8.00c at 0.40/0.68, 52% on 407 open interest. SMR 9/11 9.00c at 1.06/1.53 and the 9.50c at 0.84/1.21, both about 36% and the tightest books on the list. Several of these are affordable outright - the SOUN 8.00c is 54 at the mark, the JOBY 9.00c is 71 - so affordability is not what refuses them. The ceiling is 10% and the best quote on the board is more than three times it. That finding has now been recorded at 128.90 deployable, at 126.06 and at 109.88, which is the point at which it stops being a fact about this account's cash and becomes a fact about which instruments this rulebook can reach. Equity on the same name quotes 8.82 against 8.84. Equity is the instrument, and this run stopped arguing about it after the eighth quote.

THE STRADDLE, because it is the most useful number this run produced and it is what closed off the clean entry. Friday's pre-close handed this slot one item by name: SMCI reports 8/11 after the close, any hold opened Monday contains the print, so pull the at-the-money straddle before sizing anything. Pulled. The SMCI 2026-08-14 32 call marks 2.51 - 2.47 bid, 2.55 ask, 2,399 open interest - and the 32 put marks 2.05 - 2.00 bid, 2.10 ask, 645 open interest. That is a 4.56 straddle against a 32.21 spot: the market prices a 14.2% move on tomorrow night. SMCI is refused on that arithmetic and not on a view about the company. The rulebook stops equity at -8%. An 8% stop sits entirely inside a 14.2% expected move, which means the realistic bad case is a gap straight through it rather than a fill at it - the exit written down before entry would simply not be the exit taken, and an exit the event is priced to jump is not an exit. This is what item 3 is for, and it is worth noting it decided the trade rather than merely permitting the question: the number was pulled and then obeyed. An option on SMCI never arose, refused twice over - any 3-6 week expiry spans 8/11 and the rulebook forbids holding a contract through a print outright.

AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS FORCED. SMCI was the only name on this board with a catalyst ahead of it. The forward calendar was swept live across all twelve watched names and returns exactly one report in the window: SMCI, 8/11, pm, verified, estimate 0.88 - itself a correction to the 0.69 this board has carried since 8/7. Once the straddle refuses SMCI, there is no name left on the list to which item 1 can honestly say yes. So item 1 fails, and the mandate obliges an entry anyway.

ITEM 1, FAIL, stated plainly rather than argued around. JOBY reported 8/5 after the close. The print is three sessions old and priced. The rulebook names post-earnings DAY-2 continuation as a setup that fits; this is day 3, one session past what it names, and there is no catalyst of any kind inside a five-session hold. What is actually true about JOBY today is different and weaker: it is holding and extending a post-earnings advance while the entire complex it trades with is being unwound. On a board that is 10 red of 12, with OKLO giving back 7.7%, SOUN 6.1%, SMR 4.8%, IONQ 4.0%, MARA 4.0% and QBTS 2.5% - all of them the names that led Friday's tape - JOBY is +2.1% and through Friday's 8.72 high. That is relative strength, it is a real condition, and it is not an answer to 'why does this move meaningfully, soon'. Calling it a catalyst would be inferring one from the tape, which is the dressed-up form of 'it has been going up' that item 1 exists to stop. Marked fail.

WHAT EARNS IT ANYWAY, and the ranking, because a forced entry described as a good one corrupts the record the mandate exists to test. This is the best of a poor set and here is the set. JOBY first: it is the only name on the board that is green, liquid, affordable at meaningful size, structurally intact, and free of a print inside the hold. The structure is real rather than asserted - 8/6 was the reaction bar, gapping a 7.80 close to an 8.15 open and closing 8.23 on 49.4M shares against a month averaging roughly 35M; 8/7 continued to 8.64 on 33.6M; today extends through Friday's high while its peer group is sold. Second, UPST at 30.39, -2.2%, and it is ranked second purely for being the least damaged red name - it has no catalyst whatsoever, and the 8/5 reversal that gave back an entire earnings move on 12.3M shares against a 5.1M average is still unrepaired. Third and refused as a group, SOUN, SMR, OKLO, IONQ, QBTS, RGTI and MARA: every one is a 1-8% single-session give-back inside a complex-wide unwind, which is the first day of a decline and not the day-2/3 pullback the rulebook buys, and buying into it is the averaging-down shape RULES.md names as a setup that does not fit. SMCI is fourth and refused above on its own straddle. LEU and AMD are unreachable at one share. The setup I would rather have had is the one this board keeps not getting: a strong reaction bar, a day-2 or day-3 pullback that holds a level, and a dated catalyst still ahead. Today offers two of the three.

ITEM 2 PASSES, and it is worth being precise about why on a day like this. JOBY is +2.1%, nowhere near the +8% the rule refuses, and its own spike day was 8/4 with its reaction bar on 8/6 - both behind it. The rule's second clause, that a list green 5-10% across the board is a wait signal, does not engage today because the board is red. But item 2 is symmetrical in spirit and it is what refuses the rest of the list: a knife falling 6-8% is no more the rulebook's entry than a candle spiking 8%. Item 4 passes on real numbers - 8.82 bid against 8.84, a 0.02 spread that is 0.23% of mark, against option books on this very name quoting 75-106% this morning, on 27-83M shares a day through the last month. Item 5 passes: with no print inside the hold there is no merely-good-report risk to be caught by, and the positioning read runs the right way - JOBY is conspicuously not the crowded name today, since the crowded ones are the ones down 4-8%. Item 6 passes and the numbers are here before the entry, not after it: target 10.62 at +20%, stop 8.14 at -8%, time stop the 8/14 close at five sessions. The stop is 0.71 below the limit against a name whose recent daily range runs 0.38 to 0.67, so it sits roughly one session of noise away rather than inside it - which is the objection that killed IONQ on this board twice and it is worth confirming it does not apply here.

SIZE AND EXECUTION. Twelve shares at an 8.85 limit is 106.20 against 109.88 of settled cash - settled, on a cash account, with nothing unsettled and no good-faith exposure. One position of a two-position ceiling. The limit is set three cents above the 8.84 ask so it is marketable on a small drift rather than resting behind the market; if it fills below 8.85 the operator should re-strike both exits off the actual fill. This specification expires at 10:30 ET. THIS RUN HAS NO ORDER AUTHORITY - a human executes it or it does not happen, and if it is not executed by 10:30 it lapses rather than standing.

The two standing escalations are unchanged and untouched by this run, and both are carried forward: the publish gate cannot express an option exit at all, and three filled orders in this account carry a placed_agent of 'agentic' in an account whose mandate sets allowOrderPlacement false.
