entries.head: First hourly: nothing to exit on a flat book, the day's only specification expired unexecuted, and the account was funded ten-fold mid-session
entries.body: Fired 10:22 ET against the 10:17 slot, five minutes late, well inside the staleness guard, every quote struck live. The connector attached and the scope preflight matched the target account exactly against the connector list, with every other account discarded unread. THE EXITS ANSWER FIRST, because it is the only one this slot owes. The account is flat on a live broker read - zero equity positions, zero option positions - so there was no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window to enforce, and nothing went unenforced. That is the whole of the job and it did not come up. Positions were read from the broker rather than inferred from this repository, which matters more than usual today, because the repository would have been wrong about the balance. THE BALANCE IS THE FINDING. Settled cash reads 1009.88 against the 109.88 the open verified at 09:46 and that this board has carried through six identical reads: a difference of exactly 900.00, with buying power the same figure, nothing unsettled and no pending deposit outstanding, so it is credited and spendable rather than in flight. It cannot have come from trading. The broker returns ZERO orders of any kind in this account since 8/7 - no fill, no partial, no cancellation - and the book is flat in both asset classes, so there is no transaction to attribute it to. What remains is an operator deposit landing between 09:46 and 10:22. This run records that as a live read and declines to explain it, because inventing an intent for money that appeared is precisely the inference this board exists to refuse. IT IS ESCALATED, NOT SPENT, and the sequencing is the entire point: a roughly ten-fold increase in account size arrived in the middle of the one session slot that is forbidden to open anything, in the same hour as the only name on the board that is working. A run that treated new cash as a reason to act would be manufacturing permission out of a bank transfer. The open slot tomorrow will size against 1009.88 unless the operator says otherwise, and it should read the next finding before it does. WHAT THE DEPOSIT DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE, written down now rather than rediscovered later as a licence. The 8/5 rule that options are usually unavailable to this rulebook rested on two things, affordability and spread, and the deposit answers only affordability. Affordability had already stopped being the binding constraint: for three consecutive sessions options have been refused on SPREAD, most recently this morning at 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling across eight live quotes, several of which were affordable outright at 109.88. A larger balance does not narrow a single spread by a cent. So the deposit removes an objection that was no longer doing the work and leaves untouched the one that is actually refusing these contracts. The corollary is the part worth guarding: it would be easy, and wrong, for a future run to read 1009.88 and conclude that options are back on the table. They are not, on the only evidence this board has, and the 8/5 table in docs/RULES.md should now be read as a spread finding that happened to be discovered at a small balance. THE SPECIFICATION EXPIRED UNEXECUTED. The open published a forced 12-share JOBY entry at an 8.85 limit expiring 10:30 ET, and no order was ever placed against it - the same zero-order read that rules out a trade explaining the cash rules out an execution. JOBY is 9.05 bid against 9.06, +4.7% on the day, 2.3% above its own entry, so the limit is unfillable in the eight minutes it has left. This hourly does not re-strike it, and the reasons are worth naming individually because each is independently sufficient. Following a name that has already left the level is chasing a green candle, which docs/RULES.md lists as a setup that does not fit. Doing it now makes it a mid-session entry, which is the thing this slot exists to refuse and for which the bar is explicitly higher than at the open. And doing it today would size the chase against money that landed forty minutes ago, which is how a deposit turns into tilt in a single step. The uncomfortable part is recorded plainly rather than skipped: the forced entry was right, it would be showing a gain, and none of that is an argument for re-entering higher. Being right about a level you did not get filled at is not a position. Whether an unfilled specification discharges the daily entry mandate is a question for the retro, and this run does not pre-empt the answer - the mandate as written obliges the open slot to PUBLISH, which it did, and says nothing about whether a human executes. THE TAPE, briefly, because it is context rather than a candidate. Breadth improved from 10 red of 12 at the open to 8 red of 12, and eleven of twelve names are bid higher than they were at 09:46. That is a bounce off the opening low, not a bottom, and forty minutes of not-falling is not the day-2/3 pullback the rulebook buys. Two rows argue the unwind is unfinished: SOUN is the only name on the board lower than at the open read, -7.2% while its entire complex bounced, and UPST is within two cents of its 09:46 quote while everything around it lifted. SMCI is the strongest name at +5.7% and stays refused on its own 14.2% straddle, which strength into a print does not address. Nothing here is a mid-session entry. TWO STANDING ESCALATIONS ARE UNCHANGED and are repeated so they do not age out: the publish gate still cannot express an option exit at all, and three filled orders in this account carry a placed_agent of agentic in an account whose mandate sets allowOrderPlacement false. The deposit is now a third, and it is the one with a live consequence tomorrow morning.

grade.text: PASS, and it is the strongest single hour on this board so far. The slot's own job was empty and was answered honestly rather than skipped: flat on a live broker read, so no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window existed and none went unenforced, with the entry noting it read positions from the broker rather than from this repository - which mattered more than usual, because the repository was about to be wrong about the balance. THE ESCALATION IS THE GRADE. Settled cash read 1009.88 against the 109.88 that six identical reads had carried, a difference of exactly 900.00, credited and spendable with nothing pending. The run established what it could not be before saying what it was: the broker returned zero orders of any kind since 8/7 and the book was flat in both asset classes, so no transaction could account for it. It then declined to explain it, escalated, and did not size against it. A roughly ten-fold increase in account size arriving mid-session, in the one slot forbidden to open anything, in the same hour as the only name on the board that was working, is the exact setup in which a run manufactures permission out of a bank transfer - and this one named that shape and refused it. The operator answered the same morning that it was a deposit and that the escalation was right, but the grade does not rest on that: the reasoning was correct before the answer arrived and would have been correct had the answer never come. THE SECOND HALF IS BETTER THAN THE FIRST. It ring-fenced what the deposit does and does not license, in advance of anyone needing it: the 8/5 option finding had two halves, affordability and spread; the deposit answers only affordability; and affordability had already stopped being the binding constraint, three sessions of refusals having turned on spread, most recently 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling on contracts affordable outright. 'No balance narrows a spread' is the whole of it, and writing it down before a later run could read a bigger number as an argument is the kind of guarding this log is for. THE EXPIRED SPECIFICATION WAS HANDLED CORRECTLY AND THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART RECORDED. JOBY was 9.05 bid against the dead 8.85 limit, 2.3% through it, and the entry said plainly that the forced entry was right and would be showing a gain - then gave three independently sufficient reasons not to re-strike: chasing a name that has left the level is a setup the rulebook names as not fitting, doing it here makes it a mid-session entry where the bar is higher by design, and doing it today sizes the chase against money that landed forty minutes earlier. 'Being right about a level you did not get filled at is not a position' is the sentence the remaining six re-marks of the day vindicated. It also referred the question of whether an unfilled specification discharges the daily entry mandate to this retro instead of answering it in its own favour; it is answered in perf.json, and the answer is that publication discharges it.

entries.head: First hour with a position to check: four levels on OKLO, four clear - and the last run's evidence inverted while its conclusion held
entries.body: FOUR LEVELS, FOUR CLEAR, and that is the whole of what this slot exists to do. The account holds 2 OKLO at a 45.1499 average against a live 44.91 bid, so the position is -0.53%, 0.48 of unrealized loss on a 90.30 cost. The 54.18 target needs the bid up 20.6%. The 41.54 stop needs it down 7.5%. The time stop is the 8/14 close with today counting as session one of five. The no-fly window was re-pulled live rather than carried forward - 910 earnings events across 8/10 to 8/14 with OKLO in none of them, so its 8/7 print sits behind this hold rather than inside it, and no option is held for that rule to bite on in any case. Nothing was hit, so nothing was done and no exit specification is owed. A level hit and not acted on is the failure this slot exists to prevent; no level was hit, and the distinction between that and not having looked is the reason every number above was quoted from the bid rather than from the board. THE PROVENANCE ESCALATION IS CARRIED AND NOT COMPOUNDED. The order record was queried directly rather than inferred from a balance: exactly one order exists in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET at 45.1499 on a 45.40 limit, placed_agent 'agentic', with no specification from any run in this project behind it. Nothing further has arrived through that channel in the forty-three minutes since. The escalation stands open for the retro. This run enforces the levels on a position that exists, whoever opened it, and does not re-argue how it got there. THE CORRECTION THIS RUN OWES IS TO EVIDENCE, NOT TO A CONCLUSION. At 10:22 breadth had improved from 10 red of 12 to 8 red and that run refused to call it a bottom, saying forty minutes of less-bad is not a session of having stopped. It was right: breadth is 10 red of 12 again, nine of twelve names are bid below their 10:22 quotes, the two marginal greens flipped back - QBTS +0.05% to -1.20%, LEU +0.07% to -0.71% - and the two real ones gave back most of what they held, SMCI +5.7% to +3.7% and JOBY +4.7% to +1.6%. But the two specific tells that run offered have both inverted. SOUN, named as the cleanest evidence the give-back was unfinished precisely because it kept falling while its complex bounced, is 7.53 bid against 7.44 and is one of only three names HIGHER than at 10:22. UPST, named as the other tell for going nowhere while eleven names lifted, is the second at 30.66 against 30.37. IONQ is the third. The call held and the reasons offered for it did not, which is recorded because a read that is right for reasons that stop being true within the hour is a read that got lucky about its reasoning, and this board is worth less if it only writes down the half of that sentence that flatters it. SECOND CORRECTION, TO THIS BOARD'S OWN LEDGER. At 10:22 it wrote that the expired forced JOBY entry would be showing a gain - JOBY was 9.05 bid, 2.3% past the 8.85 limit the open published, and the note said so plainly because the forced arm is measured separately so that inconvenient facts change no rules. JOBY is 8.78 bid now, seven cents BELOW that limit, and the same specification would be showing -0.79%. Both statements were true when written. What the round trip actually demonstrates is the ground the 10:22 refusal stood on rather than an argument against it: a name that runs 2.3% past its level in forty minutes can come back through it in sixty, so re-striking upward would have been the error it looked like a missed opportunity for. Whether an 8.85 limit that never filled counts against the daily mandate at all remains the retro's call and this run does not pre-empt it. NO NEW ENTRY, and it was not close on three independent grounds. The mid-session bar is higher than the open's by design and the daily entry mandate binds the open slot, not this one. The complex resumed falling after a forty-minute bounce, and day one of a decline is the shape item 2 refuses rather than the day-2/3 pullback the rulebook buys - the deterioration this hour concentrated in the very complex the account is now long, MARA -2.1% to -4.5%, SMR -3.4% to -4.3%, OKLO -6.7% to -7.3%. And the one name on this board with a forward catalyst prints tomorrow evening against a 14.2% implied move that an 8% stop sits entirely inside, re-confirmed live on the calendar at pm timing, verified, estimate 0.88. Options stay refused on spread for a third consecutive session, which 919.58 of settled cash does nothing to narrow, because no balance narrows a spread. Deployable is 919.58 with nothing unsettled; the book is one name of four, 8.9% of account value at the bid against a 40% single-name ceiling, and one of the two the nuclear complex allows.

entries.head: Four levels clear on OKLO, and the first hour the board stopped falling is the hour the position made a new low
entries.body: FOUR LEVELS, FOUR CLEAR, AND A POSITION THAT MADE A NEW LOW FOR THE DAY WHILE THE BOARD AROUND IT STOPPED FALLING. The account holds 2 OKLO at a 45.1499 average against a live 44.27 bid: the position is -1.95%, 1.76 of unrealized loss on a 90.30 cost. The 54.18 target needs the bid up 22.4%. The 41.54 stop needs it down 6.2%. The time stop is the 8/14 close with today session one of five. No option is held, so no no-fly window can bite, and the calendar was re-pulled live rather than carried forward - 934 earnings events across 8/10 to 8/14, OKLO in none of them, SMCI on 8/11 pm verified at an 0.88 estimate the only watched name inside the window. Nothing was hit, so no exit specification is owed and none is written. THE STOP IS NOW INSIDE ONE DAY'S RANGE, AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN ACTED ON. At 11:22 the stop was 7.5% below the bid; it is 6.2% below now, on a name that has already travelled 8.57% today. A stop that sits inside a single session's realised range is a stop an ordinary continuation of the session already in progress reaches. That is a fact about the distance and not a reason to sell at -1.95%: the rulebook exits AT the level, and exiting early because the level looks reachable is a stop moved by nerves in the direction that happens to feel prudent. It is written down in advance so that if 41.54 trades this afternoon nobody has to reconstruct whether it was foreseen. THE FINDING IS A DIVERGENCE, AND IT IS THE FIRST THING TODAY THAT IS ABOUT THE POSITION RATHER THAN ABOUT THE TAPE. Every previous read this session was a story about the whole list moving together: 10 green of 12 into Friday's bell, 10 red at the open, 8 red at 10:22, 10 red again at 11:22. This hour breaks the pattern in the honest direction - breadth improves to 9 red of 12, RGTI flips green at +0.4%, and the board is exactly even hour-on-hour at six names bid higher and six lower, against nine of twelve lower last hour. IONQ, UPST, QBTS and SOUN are all firmer. Against that, OKLO fell 0.64 to 44.27 and is the worst name on this board for a fourth consecutive read. It has now declined to participate in two separate intraday bounces in its own complex. When a name sits out its complex's recoveries twice in one session, the correlation that justifies watching the complex stops covering the name, and what is left is a name-specific problem that the levels will price in their own time rather than a view this slot is entitled to act on early. NO ENTRY, AND IT WAS NOT CLOSE ON FOUR INDEPENDENT GROUNDS. The mid-session bar is higher than the open's by design and the daily entry mandate attaches to the open slot, which discharged it at 09:41. One flat hour after two falling ones is the least informative moment in a decline at which to decide the decline has ended, and it is not the day-2/3 pullback the rulebook buys. The single name with a forward catalyst is refused on a 14.2% implied move against an 8% stop, re-confirmed live on the calendar this hour. And options stay refused on spread for a fourth consecutive session, a refusal that 919.58 of settled cash does nothing to narrow, because no balance narrows a spread. THE JOBY RE-MARK IS NOW A SEQUENCE AND IT IS RECORDED IN FULL BECAUSE THE FIRST ENTRY IN IT WAS THE FLATTERING ONE. The open's forced 12-share entry at an 8.85 limit expired unexecuted at 10:30. At 10:22 this board wrote that it would be showing a gain, JOBY then 9.05 bid. At 11:22 it wrote -0.79% at 8.78. It is 8.67 bid now and the same specification would be -2.03%: three re-marks, each worse than the last. All three were true when written, none is a rule, and together they are the clearest available argument that refusing to chase the name back up through its own level at 10:22 was correct on its own terms rather than lucky. THE PROVENANCE ESCALATION IS CARRIED A THIRD HOUR, UNCHANGED AND UNCOMPOUNDED. The order record was queried directly rather than inferred from the balance: exactly one order exists in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET at 45.1499 on a 45.40 limit with placed_agent 'agentic', and no run in this project published a specification behind it. Nothing new has arrived through that channel in the hundred minutes since. That is the retro's to answer; this slot enforces the levels on a position that exists, whoever opened it. state.json re-struck in full on 12:22 bids across all twelve names. Deployable is 919.58 settled with nothing pending, and against the 2026-08-10 concentration rule the book is one name of four, 8.8% of account value at the bid against a 40% ceiling, and one of the two the nuclear complex allows.

It also noticed that this is the same shape as its own SMCI refusal - a stop sitting inside the move the instrument is actually making - and that the argument which refuses an entry does not, under this rulebook, close an existing position. Naming a risk in advance and then not letting the naming become the action is the hard part, and both halves were done. THE moves.json PASS IS PROCEDURAL AND IT IS THE ONE MOST RUNS WOULD HAVE HALF-DONE. Refreshing spot alone would have left a 14.2% ratio struck against a 32.21 spot that no longer exists sitting beside a 31.70 spot that does: internally inconsistent, and wrong in the flattering direction. The straddle was re-pulled at the same instant as the spot, both legs quoted with open interest and deltas, and the composition flip was correctly attributed to spot crossing the 32 strike rather than to the market taking a side, with near-symmetric deltas cited as the evidence. The refusal is unchanged at 13.7%, and the entry says half a point never came near the gap between 8 and 13.7. THE FLAG, and its first real movement. This slot was flagged on 8/5, 8/6 and 8/7 for writing and pushing with no re-read between, and the 8/7 retro named two acceptable remedies: re-read the account immediately before pushing, or drop the finality claim. It also matters more this time than it ever has, because the board went live describing a HELD position rather than a flat one, and a held book can be falsified by a sale as well as by a purchase. This retro can say from the order record rather than from assumption that nothing filled in that window - exactly one order exists in this account since 8/7 - so the exposure cost nothing today. entries.head: OKLO held a second night as a decision; the SMCI straddle finally re-struck as a pair, and it widened
entries.body: FOUR LEVELS CHECKED AGAINST A LIVE 46.99 BID, FOUR CLEAR, AND THE HOLD IS THE OUTPUT. 2 OKLO at a 45.1499 average: +4.08%, 3.68 of unrealized gain on a 90.30 cost. The 54.18 target needs the bid up 15.30%. The 41.54 stop needs it down 11.60%. The time stop is the 8/14 close with today session two of five, so two sessions remain after tonight. Nothing was hit, nothing is sold, no exit specification is owed. THE LEVEL THAT WOULD CHANGE THE HOLD IS 41.54 AND IT IS WRITTEN DOWN TONIGHT RATHER THAN INHERITED FROM LAST NIGHT'S ENTRY. That is not ceremony. The 8/10 rule says a hold is not a decision made once, and the way that rule fails in practice is a run reading yesterday's number, agreeing with it, and calling the agreement a decision. So: if 41.54 trades it is sold, if 54.18 trades it is sold, if neither happens by the 8/14 close the time stop sells it, and none of the three is negotiable by a better story tomorrow morning. BOTH SAME-DAY EXIT TRIGGERS WERE RUN LIVE AND BOTH ARE CLEAN, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The option position list was queried and is empty, so no no-fly window closes on anything today - that is the check that forces a same-day sale when a print lands before a contract expires, and it is written out because a check nobody logged is a check nobody did. And no print lands on the underlying tonight: 760 calendar events across 8/11 to 8/15 pulled live, OKLO in none of them, SMCI the only watched name inside the window. No straddle was owed on this position and none is claimed - the rule that no straddle pulled means no earnings hold is satisfied here by there being no earnings, which is the only honest way to satisfy it without a quote. WHAT IS DIFFERENT FROM LAST NIGHT'S HOLD IS WORTH STATING PRECISELY, BECAUSE IT IS TEMPTING TO STATE IT AS PROGRESS. On 8/10 this slot held the same position and wrote down that a repeat of that session's -7.44% would land at 41.49, THROUGH the 41.54 stop, so the honest description was one ordinary session of room rather than 7.3% of it. Tonight the same arithmetic from 46.99 lands at 43.49, which clears the stop. The level did not move; the price did. The stop is 11.60% away, the widest it has read since the fill for a fourth consecutive hour - and it already narrowed 0.39 points in the fifteen minutes between the last hourly and this run, which is the cleanest demonstration available that distance-to-stop is a fact about price rather than a cushion anyone earned. Last night's run named a risk that did not arrive; that is not evidence it was wrong to name it, and tonight's wider stop is not evidence this hold is safer. Both are descriptions of where the price happens to be. NOTHING WAS OPENED, AND ON THIS SLOT THAT IS THE HARDEST LINE OF THE DAY TO HOLD RATHER THAN THE EASIEST. The pre-close may not open a position in the last thirty minutes. The daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot, and today the open slot fired 247 minutes late and closed at the staleness guard with nothing published - so unlike 8/10, when the mandate discharged at 09:41 with the forced JOBY specification, tonight it goes unmet and this is the last run that could have pretended otherwise. Every earlier slot today could truthfully say the mandate was someone else's to discharge. This one is last, and it says instead that it is not discharging it: a rule that forbids opening in the final thirty minutes is not suspended by a mandate that went unmet earlier in the day. An entry written here would have been an open-slot entry wearing a 15:33 timestamp, which is the same corruption of the record the guard refused at 13:40 reached by a slower route, and it would have been the single easiest thing available to make the day look complete. 2026-08-11 closes with no specification and the reason on the record rather than inferred from an empty log tomorrow. THE SMCI PAIR WAS RE-STRUCK AFTER THREE RUNS CORRECTLY REFUSED TO HALF-REFRESH IT, AND THE RESULT CUTS AGAINST WHAT A HALF-REFRESH WOULD HAVE IMPLIED. moves.json had carried Friday's 31.70 spot and 0.137 ratio since 15:35 on 8/10. Three separate runs today named that as the file's one stale number and declined to re-mark spot alone, because dividing a Friday straddle by a Tuesday spot makes the implied range wrong in the flattering direction - the exact failure that file's comment warns about. Re-struck now inside three seconds: 31.34 spot at 19:36:39 UTC, the 8/14 31.50 call at 2.215 and the put at 2.300 quoted 19:36:32 to 19:36:38, a 4.515 straddle and a 14.4% implied move. Had spot alone been refreshed, the row would have read 13.7% against 31.34 - LOWER - and the truth is that the implied move WIDENED. THE RECORDED STRIKE MOVED FROM 32 TO 31.50 AND BOTH ARE PUBLISHED, WHICH IS THE POINT. 31.50 is the at-the-money strike at a 31.34 spot and 32 is 0.66 away, so the rulebook's ATM straddle is the 31.50 one. But switching strikes silently would have made the series incomparable and hidden the widening inside a definitional change, so the 32 straddle was quoted in the same window: 4.590 on 31.34, 14.6%, against 13.7% at Friday's close and 14.2% Friday morning. On a constant strike the move widened 0.9 points into the print. One honest complication, recorded rather than smoothed: the two tests of which strike is really the money disagree. By distance to spot, 31.50 wins. By delta symmetry, 32 wins - its 0.493 call against a -0.507 put is nearer neutral than 31.50's 0.528 and -0.473. That is the forward sitting slightly above spot and nothing more, it changes no decision, and it is written down so a later run does not rediscover it and mistake it for a finding. The refusal is unchanged and is now further from close than at any earlier read: an 8% equity stop inside a 14.4% expected move is a stop the event gaps rather than fills. NOTHING WAS PRUNED, AND THE HANDOFF INTO THIS SLOT ASKED FOR SOMETHING THAT COULD NOT BE DONE. The 15:21 hourly handed this run the pruning of the SMCI row 'once tonight's print has passed'. The print is after the 16:00 close; this run fires at 15:33. The print cannot pass inside this window, and removing a catalyst that has not happened is the inverse of the error this file guards against. The row stays with both numbers current, the board renders it PASSED overnight, the validator does not warn for two days, and the 8/12 open owns the prune and the post-print branch already written down beside it. The forward calendar was swept live across all twelve watched names and SMCI remains the only one with a catalyst in the window, so the file is complete as well as current. A FINDING THIS BOARD PUBLISHED TWO RUNS AGO IS RETRACTED, WHICH IS THE ONLY ITEM HERE THAT COSTS ANYTHING TO WRITE. The 14:21 run led its entry with nuclear dispersion at a 7.25-point spread and called it 'the hour's one real finding'. The series now reads 6.62 at 13:41, 7.25 at 14:22, 6.83 at 15:21 and 6.58 now - SMR +6.32%, OKLO +5.62%, LEU -0.26%. The spread is TIGHTER than it was before the finding was announced. So it was noise sampled at its peak, and the 15:21 run's instinct to soften it was right but too gentle. What survives is only the narrow claim that this complex does not move as one thing intraday, which was true before the excursion and after it. What is retired is any directional story about the dispersion. The standing tiebreak says the number decides, and it binds this board's own theses harder than anyone else's precisely because these are the ones it wants to defend. The two-per-complex cap is untouched throughout: it guards stops gapping together in a decline, which 8/10 demonstrated across twelve names and three unrelated stories, and an up-move that disperses and re-converges is not that case. THE PROVENANCE ESCALATION IS CARRIED AN ELEVENTH TIME, UNCHANGED AND UNCOMPOUNDED: exactly one order in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET on 8/10 at 45.1499 against a 45.40 limit, placed_agent agentic, with no specification from any run here behind it. Queried directly rather than inferred, for the eleventh consecutive time. It is the retro's to answer; this slot's job was the levels on a position that exists, whoever opened it, and the decision about whether it survives the night. Deployable is 919.58 settled with nothing pending.

Publishing an entry here would have been the single easiest way to make 2026-08-11 look complete, and refusing it costs a visible zero on the board. THE SMCI PAIR IS THE PROCEDURAL HIGH POINT. Spot and straddle re-struck inside three seconds after three runs correctly refused to half-refresh them, and the result cuts against what a half-refresh would have implied - the implied move WIDENED to 14.4% where a spot-only update would have printed 13.7% and shown it falling. THE ONE FLAG IS MECHANICAL AND IS NOT THIS ENTRY'S REASONING. The pre-close write-then-push gap stands for a fourth session: last quote 19:36:39Z, commit 15:42:19 ET, six minutes forty with no re-read, on a board that went live describing a HELD position. Nothing filled in that window - the broker returns zero orders in this account on 8/11, so this retro can say it from the record rather than assume it - and the 8/5 fill 84 seconds after the equivalent read is why the measurement keeps being taken. entries.head: FORCED on item 2: buy 6 SMCI at 39.64. The only dated catalyst on the board, bought on the day-2 extension instead of the pullback that never came
entries.body: THE ENTRY IS FORCED AND THE FAILING ITEM IS 2, WHICH IS THE ITEM THAT MATTERS MOST ON A DAY LIKE THIS. SMCI reported 8/11 after the close and 8/12 gapped it from a 31.60 close to 37.61 - +19.0% on 165,736,379 shares against a 56.6M two-week average, about three times normal participation. Today is day 2 and it is +5.32% on the bid at 39.61, having opened 38.24 and run to 39.82. The rulebook does not buy that. It buys the day-2/3 PULLBACK after strength, and there has been no pullback of any size: today's session low of 38.20 sits ABOVE yesterday's 37.61 close, and a 39.64 entry is 25.4% above the pre-print 31.60. This is extension, it is the thing item 2 exists to refuse, and it is marked fail rather than argued into a pass on the technicality that +5.32% is not +8%. THE BRANCH THAT DECIDES THIS WAS WRITTEN BEFORE THE PRINT AND IT ANSWERS AGAINST ME. data/moves.json has carried since 8/11, in advance of the event, the branch 'SMCI still wanted after the print - re-approach from 8/12, on the reaction bar rather than into it', with the explicit qualifier 'the reaction day is not the entry, the day-2/3 pullback that holds is'. That is this board's own instruction, written when the outcome was unknown, and it is the cleanest possible test of whether this project's process survives contact with a move it likes. It does not survive it cleanly. The branch says wait; the entry is published anyway under the daily mandate, marked forced, with the branch quoted rather than deleted. WHY THIS AND NOT SOMETHING QUIETER - THE RANKING, WITH THE REFUSALS ATTACHED. The earnings calendar was pulled live at 502 events across 8/13 to 8/19 and NOT ONE of the twelve watched names appears in it. So SMCI's 8/11 print is the only dated catalyst inside a five-session hold anywhere on this board, and every alternative fails item 1 outright rather than item 2. Second: IONQ at a 46.89 bid, +3.74%, refused because it reported 8/5 and six-session-old news carries nothing forward - 'it has been going up' is named in the rulebook as not a catalyst. Third: UPST at 29.35, +0.86%, the cheapest non-chase on the list and refused twice over, once on item 1 at seven sessions past its print and once on structure, still below both the 30.20 close and the 30.32 pre-earnings level the 8/6 attempt failed at, now a fourth session under them. AMD at 496.00 is refused mechanically at 49.0% of the account against a 40% single-name ceiling. SMR and LEU are nuclear, where the OKLO position already holds one of two slots, and both are past their prints anyway. THE CHOICE WAS BETWEEN TWO FAILURES AND I TOOK THE ONE I THINK IS SMALLER. Fail item 1 on a quiet name with no reason to move, or fail item 2 on the only name that answers 'why does this move meaningfully, soon'. This board already has the first experiment on the record: the 8/10 JOBY entry failed item 1, was published forced, and expired unfilled. A dated catalyst bought too high is a different error from no catalyst at all - the first can still be right about direction and merely wrong about price, the second has nothing to be right about. I do not claim that makes it a good entry. It is the best of a poor set and the set was poor because the calendar is empty. ITEM 5 IS LOGGED 'ne' AND THAT IS A HOLE, NOT A PASS. The rule as written guards buying INTO a print with crowded bulls and raised targets, and there is no print ahead, so on its own terms it does not apply. But the post-print analogue is real and is the single strongest argument against this trade: a +19% reaction may already contain the whole of the good news, and the marginal buyer at 39.64 is paying for a beat that everyone has now read. I have no positioning data, no revision data and no short-interest read in this run, so I am not answering that question, and I am not going to manufacture a pass out of price action to fill the box. An unlogged check counts as not done; this one is logged as not evaluated, which is the honest label and is a real gap in the entry. THE EXITS, WRITTEN NOW. Limit 39.64, which is the live ask against a 39.61 bid - a marketable limit rather than a resting one, and deliberately so. Target 47.57, which is +20% and is the rulebook's take-profit, not more. Stop 36.47, which is -8%. Time stop the 8/19 close, five sessions counting today as session 1. Six shares, 237.84, which is 23.5% of a 1012.33 account against a 40% single-name ceiling and 919.58 of settled cash - above the ~10% floor where a winner cannot move the day, below the ceiling where one name becomes the account. Complex ai-hardware, which this book has never held, so nothing in it gaps with the nuclear position. Risk at the stop is 19.03. I DID NOT PRICE THE LIMIT WHERE THE SETUP I WANTED WOULD HAVE FILLED, AND THAT REFUSAL IS THE POINT. The honest better entry is a hold of the 38.20 session low or a fade toward 37.61 on lighter volume. I could have written that limit, called item 2 a pass, and published a specification that almost certainly does not fill inside a 44-minute window on a stock trading 39.61 and rising. That is standing aside wearing the mandate's clothes, and it would have corrupted the record in exactly the way the mandate warns about - a forced entry described as a good one. The limit is where the stock actually is. THE -8% STOP IS TIGHT FOR THIS NAME RIGHT NOW AND I AM SAYING SO BEFORE THE OUTCOME. SMCI's session range today is already 38.20 to 39.82, 4.2% wide, and its 30-day option IV reads 78.5%. An 8% stop is about two of today's ranges. The rulebook fixes it at -8% and the rulebook wins over my preference, but a stop that noise can reach is a real weakness of this entry and it belongs in the pre-trade record rather than in the retro that discovers it. OPTIONS CLEARED THE 10% SPREAD TEST FOR THE FIRST TIME ON THIS BOARD, AND I STILL BOUGHT THE STOCK. Three SMCI 2026-09-18 calls were pulled from the live chain and quoted: the 38 strike 4.65/4.85 on 4,213 open interest, delta 0.625, spread 4.21% of mark; the 39 strike 4.15/4.40 on 1,635 open interest, delta 0.584, 5.85%; the 40 strike 3.75/3.95 on 14,793 open interest and 535 traded, delta 0.544, 5.19%. All three clear the 10% ceiling, the 0.40 delta floor and the 3-6 week window at 36 days out, and the print is behind them so the no-earnings-hold rule is satisfied. That retires a claim this project has carried since 8/5 - options were refused three sessions running on spread, most recently at 36% of mark, and docs/RULES.md called it 'the shape of the universe, not three unlucky picks'. The universe it actually described was SOUN, SMR and UPST. The first liquid chain this board has examined clears easily, so the true statement is that the names this account was looking at had unusable option markets, not that options are unusable at this size. THE CONTRACT WAS REFUSED ON ARITHMETIC, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT REFUSAL FROM THE OLD ONE AND HAS TO BE SEPARATED FROM IT. One 40-strike contract at the 3.85 mark costs 385.00 - 38.0% of a 1012.33 account, two points under the 40% ceiling - and the rulebook's -40% option stop puts 154.00 at risk, 15.2% of the account, behind a thesis I have just marked forced. Against that the six shares risk 19.03. The decay is the other half: theta reads -0.0556 a day, so five flat sessions cost about 10% of premium before direction enters into it, and vega 0.0496 against a still-elevated 78.5% post-print IV costs roughly another 17% on a 13-point volatility decay that is the normal course after an event. The contract can lose a quarter of its value while the thesis is neither right nor wrong. The equity loses only when I am wrong about direction, and direction is the only thing this thesis claims. Putting 15.2% of the account behind a forced thesis in the instrument that also bleeds sideways is the trade I would not defend to the grader. BREADTH IS 11 GREEN OF 12 AND I AM BUYING INTO IT, WHICH IS THE LAST CAUTION. Only LEU is red, at -0.12%. Item 2's second sentence - the whole list green 5-10% is a wait signal - does not fire on its terms, because the magnitudes run +0.13% to +5.32% and only SMCI is above 4%; I am not stretching it into a refusal it does not support. What is true is that on a tape where eleven of twelve names are up, most of any single name's move is the tape, and the portion of SMCI's +5.32% that belongs to SMCI is smaller at 09:46 than it looks. That is precisely why the catalyst has to carry this position rather than the momentum, and why the time stop is doing more work here than usual: if the print is not still driving this name by the 8/19 close, the thesis was wrong regardless of where the price sits. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS ENTRY WRONG, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME. A close back below 37.61 - yesterday's close - would say the gap is being filled and the reaction is being sold, and that is well above my 36.47 stop, so I would expect the stop to be reached in that scenario rather than avoided. A day-3 or day-4 fade on rising volume says the same thing louder. Conversely, a hold above 38.20 with the advance continuing on above-average volume is the thesis working. I am not claiming a probability on either; I am recording which observations would settle it, so the grader is marking a prediction rather than a story.

entries.head: Held OKLO on all four levels, and refused to re-strike the SMCI entry that is about to expire unfilled
entries.body: THE EXIT DECISION FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THIS SLOT'S ONLY MANDATORY OUTPUT. All four OKLO levels were checked against a live 45.98 bid and all four clear: 2 shares at a 45.1499 average, +1.84%, target 54.18 a further 17.83% away, stop 41.54 a further 9.66% away, time stop the 8/14 close with today session 4 of 5. THE REAL DECISION OF THIS RUN IS THE ONE NOT TO ACT. The 09:40 open published a forced 6-share SMCI buy at a 39.64 limit expiring 10:30. At 10:21 SMCI is 41.17 bid against yesterday's 37.61 close, +9.47%, so the market is 3.86% through the limit and the broker shows zero equity orders in this account today. The specification will lapse unfilled with nine minutes left on it, and this run declines to re-strike it. THE REASONING, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME IS KNOWN. Three separate rules point the same way and none of them is a judgement call. First, the daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text and explicitly leaves the mid-session default at no trade with a HIGHER bar for a new entry; the mandate is already discharged for 2026-08-13 by a spec that was live and executable when written, and a spec that lapses because the market ran away from it is a missed fill, not an undischarged mandate. Second, the entry was already forced on item 2 at 39.64 - 25.4% above the pre-print 31.60 with no pullback - and re-striking at 41.17 makes it 30.3% above, which is the same failure bought worse. Third, the standing tiebreak says the number decides: 41.17 is not 39.64, and this board's own precedent is the 8/10 JOBY spec, which expired unfilled at 8.85, was deliberately not re-priced into strength, and was shown across thirteen reads to have cost the account nothing. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS WRONG, NAMED IN ADVANCE SO THE RETRO CAN GRADE IT RATHER THAN RE-ARGUE IT. If SMCI closes the week meaningfully above 41.17, this run will have watched the only dated catalyst on the board walk away over 1.53 points, and the honest reading then is that the open's limit was struck too tight under a mandate that forces an entry into a name already extended. That is a real cost and it is not hedged here. What it is not is a reason to buy at 10:21: the alternative on offer was never 'the same trade slightly worse', it was a trade whose one failing checklist item fails harder at every price this run could have paid. THE CANDIDATE TABLE WAS DELIBERATELY NOT REFRESHED. This run quoted the two names it owed a number on - the held position and the specified name - and left the other ten at the open's 09:46 strike with the timestamp saying so. Refreshing half a board and publishing it under one 'as of' is the error that makes a board read as internally consistent when it is not.

entries.head: FORCED on item 1: buy 8 UPST at 30.59. Nothing on the board has a catalyst, so the entry goes to the one setup the rulebook names by title rather than to a third-day extension this board refused five times yesterday at lower prices
entries.body:
THE MANDATE IS DISCHARGED AND THE FAILURE IS ITEM 1, ON EVERY CANDIDATE RATHER THAN ON THIS ONE. The earnings calendar was pulled live across 2026-08-14 to 2026-08-20 and not one of the twelve watched names appears in it. There is no dated catalyst anywhere on this board. So item 1 does not distinguish between candidates today - it fails on all of them - and the choice was never 'which name has a reason to move', it was 'which name is the least bad thing to own for five sessions without one'. That is worth stating plainly, because it is a weaker position than yesterday's, where at least one name answered item 1.

WHAT UPST HAS INSTEAD OF A CATALYST IS A SETUP THE RULEBOOK LISTS BY NAME. 'Breakout pullbacks' is one of three setups under 'Setups that fit'. On 8/13 UPST opened 29.19, ran to a 31.35 high and closed 30.97 on 4.85M shares against a 4.30M thirty-day average - a +6.4% session that reclaimed BOTH structural lines this board has been tracking since the 8/6 attempt failed: the 30.20 close it broke and the 30.32 pre-earnings level. Today it has pulled back, low 30.45, and is 30.57 bid at -1.29%, which is above both reclaimed lines. That is the shape the rulebook buys: not the up day, the day after it, with the level holding.

IT ALSO RETIRES THE SPECIFIC REASON THIS NAME WAS REFUSED YESTERDAY. The 8/13 open ranked UPST third and refused it on two counts: no catalyst, and 'still below BOTH structural lines the 8/6 attempt failed at, now closing a fourth session under them'. The second count is no longer true - the tape resolved it that afternoon. The first count still stands and is what makes this entry forced. A refusal whose stated reason has half-expired should be re-read rather than repeated, and this is the re-read.

WHY NOT SMCI, WHICH IS THE ENTRY THIS BOARD MADE YESTERDAY. SMCI is 40.26 bid, +2.81%, and it is refused today on a number rather than on a view. Three things, in order of weight. First: the entry is 27.4% above the 31.60 pre-print close and there has still been no pullback, which is the identical item-2 failure the 8/13 spec was forced on, only larger. Second, and this is the one that decides it: this board refused SMCI five separate times yesterday at 39.65, 39.87, 40.09, 39.87 and 39.41, every one of them BELOW today's bid, each time on that same item-2 reasoning. Buying it higher today would reverse five documented refusals, and reversing a refusal requires new information. Third: there is no new information, and what the tape did add points the other way - 8/13 touched 42.31 and closed 39.16, a 7.4% fade off the high on 122.8M shares. A name that gave back its whole range into the close is not a name that has resolved its extension. Under the 2026-08-10 standing tiebreak the number decides and the narrative is discarded; the number here is that today's entry is strictly worse than five entries this board already declined.

AND WHY THAT REVERSES YESTERDAY'S RANKING LOGIC, SAID OUT LOUD RATHER THAN QUIETLY. The 8/13 spec chose the item-2 failure over the item-1 failure on the reasoning that item 1 'is the more fundamental question'. I am choosing the other way today and the record deserves the reason: yesterday item 1 was ANSWERABLE - SMCI's print was two sessions old and the day-2 continuation is a setup the rulebook lists. Today it is answerable by nobody, so the item-1 failure is no longer a choice between a name with a catalyst and a name without one; it is the floor under every candidate. Once item 1 fails regardless, the tiebreak moves to which entry the rest of the checklist can defend, and a name passing 2, 4 and 6 on a listed setup beats a name failing 2 by a wider margin than it did yesterday. If that reasoning is wrong, it is wrong in a way the record can now check against both entries.

THE REST OF THE FIELD, RANKED, AND ALL OF IT POOR. IONQ 45.93 bid +2.11%, seven sessions past its print, nothing ahead - item 1 fails and it has no setup to put in its place. AMD 496.13 is refused mechanically before any view: one share is 49.0% of the account against the 40% single-name ceiling. RGTI 19.07 +2.42% and QBTS 21.22 +1.53% are both a week past their prints and are moving with the tape. SMR 9.75 and LEU 194.42 sit in the nuclear complex the OKLO position half-fills and are past their prints regardless. MARA 9.14 and SOUN 7.53 have neither a catalyst nor a structure. JOBY 8.07 is the weakest name on the board at -2.30% and the dead 8.85 specification from 8/10 is now -8.85% against it. This is a poor set and UPST is the best of it, not a good entry.

OPTIONS WERE PRICED LIVE AND REFUSED ON THE SPREAD, WHICH IS THE THIRD TIME THIS FINDING HAS BEEN NARROWED. Three UPST 2026-09-18 calls, 35 days out: the 27.5 strike 3.85/4.85 is 23.0% of mark, the 30 strike 2.41/2.71 is 11.7% on 11,609 open interest and 0.590 delta, the 32.5 strike 1.43/1.65 is 14.3% on 0.417 delta. The tightest misses a 10% ceiling by 1.7 points. Worth recording precisely because it is close: UPST quoted 25.5% of mark on 8/5 and quotes 11.7% now, so the standing finding is not that this chain is unusable, it is that this chain is nearly usable and still is not. No balance and no narrowing narrows it the rest of the way. Equity risks 19.60 at its stop and loses only on direction; the contract would risk 40% of a 256.00 premium on a thesis that is already forced.

SIZE, AND THE EXITS, STRUCK BEFORE ENTRY. 8 shares at a 30.59 limit is 244.72, 24.2% of a 1012.81 account - inside the 40% single-name ceiling and above the ~10% floor where a full winner cannot move the day. Target 36.71 is +20%. Stop 28.14 is -8%, and it sits 1.0% below the 28.41 low of 7/22, which is the nearest structure underneath rather than a number chosen to be comfortable. Time stop is the 8/20 close, five sessions counting today. UPST is tagged fintech, a complex this book has never held, so the two-per-complex cap is nowhere near binding beside the nuclear OKLO position and no stop in this book gaps with another.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS WRONG, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME. The honest case against it is that a breakout pullback with no catalyst is a chart pattern, and this rulebook's own item 1 says 'it has been going up' is not a reason. UPST's reclaim was a single session; one session above a line it spent four sessions below is thin evidence that the line has changed sides, and the -8% stop is only 1.3% below yesterday's 30.13 close-to-low excursion in percentage terms, which means ordinary noise in this name can reach it. If the 30.20/30.32 shelf fails and the stop takes it out inside two sessions, the correct reading is not bad luck - it is that a setup without a catalyst had nothing to hold it up, and the mandate bought a chart because the board had nothing else to buy. That is the specific thing this entry is testing, and it is what the grader should mark it against.

ITEM 5 IS LOGGED 'ne' AND IT IS A REAL GAP RATHER THAN A FORMALITY. The rule guards against crowding into a print, and there is no print ahead, so its stated case does not arise. But the honest version of item 5 here - whether a name that just reclaimed a broken level is being bought alongside everyone else who watched it reclaim - is a question this run has no positioning data to answer, and it did not invent one.

THE TIME STOP IS THE ONE LIVE LEVEL AND THIS RUN DELIBERATELY DOES NOT FIRE IT. Today is session 5 of 5 and the level written at entry is the 8/14 CLOSE. An hourly that sells at 10:21 has not enforced the time stop; it has substituted a different and earlier exit for the one the position was entered under, and done so on the argument that the day will end - which is true at every hour and therefore justifies selling at any of them. The rule this board keeps is that levels are struck at entry and enforced as written, and 'the close' is as much a written level as 41.54 is. The open handed this to the pre-close in advance rather than in hindsight and the handoff stands. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS HOUR ACT, STATED SO THE NEXT ONE INHERITS IT: 54.18 or 41.54 printing on the bid. Recording that UPST is currently above its limit as though it were a verdict would be the seventh instance of the behaviour that finding closed. Its verdict belongs to the retro. THE CANDIDATE BOARD IS NOT RE-STRUCK AND THE REASON IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT AS A GAP. The twelve rows in state.json carry the open's 09:44 bids inside a six-second window, which is what makes them comparable to each other. Re-quoting the three names this run had reason to touch would leave a board of two timestamps reading as one, which is the same defect as the 8/13 pre-close publishing a 15:35 bid as a close. entries.head: The position crossed below its cost and no exit is due, because zero is not a level this book defends
entries.body: NO EXIT WAS DUE AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OUTPUT OF THIS SLOT. Fired 14:21 against the 14:17 slot, four minutes late and inside the 20-minute guard. The scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly against the connector list and every other account was discarded unread. THREE OKLO LEVELS CHECKED ON A LIVE 44.93 BID, ALL CLEAR. 2 shares at 45.1499: -0.49%, an unrealized LOSS of 0.44 on a 90.30 cost, 89.86 at the bid and 8.90% of a 1009.46 account. The 54.18 target needs a further 20.59%; the 41.54 stop needs 7.55% down. Option positions queried live and empty, so no no-fly window closes on anything. THE ONE GENUINELY NEW FACT THIS HOUR IS THE SIGN. The position has been green at every reading since the 8/10 fill and is now red: 46.90 at the open, then 46.57, 45.96, 45.77, 45.29, 44.93 - 1.64 of bid across four hours, +3.15% decaying through +1.79%, +1.37% and +0.31% to -0.49%, and -3.27% against the 46.45 close. It is new as a fact about the account and it is not new as an input to a decision, and keeping those two apart is the entire job. THE BOOK DOES NOT CONTAIN THE SIGN. Every exit this rulebook defines is a number: +20% take-profit, -8% equity stop, ~5 sessions, the option no-fly window. None of them is 'the position went red'. The stop is 41.54, struck at entry off the 45.1499 fill, and the bid is 7.55% clear of it. If crossing cost were an exit, every position would carry an implicit 0% stop, no thesis would ever be given the room the -8% was chosen to give it, and the -8% would be decoration. Selling here would set the stop to the entry price after the fact - the same defect as widening a stop, pointed the other way, and no more defensible for being the conservative direction. There was also no gain to protect: the take-profit was never within 20% of being touched, so nothing this slot was entitled to defend has been given up. THE TIME STOP IS THE LIVE LEVEL AND THIS RUN AGAIN DOES NOT FIRE IT EARLY. Today is session 5 of 5 and the level written at entry is the 8/14 CLOSE. Four earlier runs today refused to contract it and the reasoning is unchanged rather than re-derived: an hourly that sells at 14:21 has not enforced the time stop, it has substituted a nearer exit on the argument that the day will end, which is true at every hour and therefore justifies selling at any of them. What is new is the temptation, not the argument. A red position at session 5 of 5 with roughly 70 minutes left is the most persuasive occasion this week to make an exception, and the smallness of the gap is the tell: if selling now and selling as written are nearly the same trade, then patience costs nearly nothing and the rule is nearly free to keep. Rules are not kept on the days they are cheap and abandoned on the days they are not; that is the mechanism by which a rulebook stops existing. The 2026-08-10 change says the time stop is not extendable by conviction, and the symmetric reading is that it is not contractable by impatience either. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS HOUR ACT, UNCHANGED SINCE 10:21: 54.18 or 41.54 printing on the bid. Neither is reachable from here, so the calendar closes this position rather than the tape, and the pre-close should expect to sell 2 shares at the bid. THE UPST SPECIFICATION IS DEAD AND DRIFTING BACK TOWARD ITS OWN LIMIT, WHICH IS NOT A REVIVAL. Zero equity orders in this account all session, re-checked live. UPST is 30.68 bid against the dead 30.59 limit, 0.29% above it and -0.94% on the day, the closest it has come since expiry. A limit that expired is not restored by the tape crossing it again, and re-striking on price movement alone - with the thesis still forced on item 1 and no catalyst since - is exactly the chase this slot's raised bar exists to refuse. Its grade belongs to the retro. NO NEW ENTRY: the mandate binds the open slot by its own text and was discharged at 09:44, and the default here is no trade. Actions 0.

The graded decision is the refusal to treat the position crossing its own cost as an exit, and the entry does the hard thing - it names the sign flip as the most loaded print of the day, then separates the fact from the input to the decision and keeps them apart, which it correctly calls the entire job. entries.head: The last hourly refuses to contract the time stop by nine minutes, and the dead UPST limit turns marketable without turning live
entries.body:
NO EXIT WAS DUE AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OUTPUT OF THIS SLOT. Fired 15:21 against the 15:17 slot, four minutes late and inside the 20-minute guard, and this is the last hourly of the session. The scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly against the connector list and every other account was discarded unread. THREE OKLO LEVELS CHECKED ON A LIVE 44.58 BID, ALL CLEAR. 2 shares at 45.1499: -1.26%, an unrealized LOSS of 1.14 on a 90.30 cost, 89.16 at the bid and 8.84% of a 1008.79 account. The 54.18 target needs a further 21.53%; the 41.54 stop needs 6.82% down. Option positions queried live and empty, so no no-fly window closes on anything.

SIX CONSECUTIVE LOWER HOURS, AND THE RIGHT PLACE TO PUT THAT FACT IS THE TIME STOP RATHER THAN THE PRICE STOP. 46.90 at the open, then 46.57, 45.96, 45.77, 45.29, 44.93, 44.58 - 1.99 of bid across five hours, +3.15% decaying through +1.79%, +1.37%, +0.31% and -0.49% to -1.26%, and -4.03% against the 46.45 close. The loss has more than doubled in the hour since the sign flipped. That is a real signal and it says something specific: a position that has drifted one direction for six hours on its fifth session is a thesis that did not work. The rulebook already has an instrument for exactly that reading, and it is the ~5 session time stop, which fires today. What the drift is NOT is evidence about the 41.54 stop, which is 6.82% away and was struck at entry off the 45.1499 fill. Reading a slow bleed as a stop hit is how a stop stops being a number.

THE LAST HOUR IS THE EASIEST ONE TO MAKE AN EXCEPTION IN, WHICH IS WHY IT IS REFUSED HERE TOO. The level written at entry is the 8/14 CLOSE. Five earlier runs today refused to contract it and the argument is unchanged rather than re-derived: an hourly that sells at 15:21 has not enforced the time stop, it has substituted a nearer exit on the reasoning that the day will end - true at every hour, and therefore a licence to sell at any of them. What is different this hour is only that the substitution has almost no cost: nine minutes and one slot separate this read from the pre-close. That smallness is an argument for the rule being cheap to keep, not for it being optional to keep. A rule kept only when it is free is not a rule, and the 2026-08-10 change that says the time stop is not extendable by conviction reads symmetrically - it is not contractable by impatience either, least of all in the final hour when the impatience is nearly costless and therefore nearly invisible.

THE HANDOFF, WRITTEN EXPLICITLY BECAUSE NO FURTHER HOURLY WILL RUN. Unless 54.18 or 41.54 prints on the bid first, the pre-close sells 2 shares at the bid on the time stop, session 5 of 5 from the 8/10 fill. Neither of those two numbers is reachable from 44.58 in nine minutes, so the honest expectation is that the calendar closes this position at a small loss rather than the tape closing it at a level. That was already the expectation at 10:21 when the position was +3.15%, and it is worth noting that the expectation did not change while the number moved 4.4 points - which is the test of whether a level was actually written down in advance or merely narrated afterward.

THE DEAD UPST LIMIT BECAME MARKETABLE THIS HOUR AND IS STILL DEAD. UPST is 30.49 bid / 30.52 ask. The ask is now BELOW the 30.59 limit the open published, so the specification that expired unfilled at 10:30 would fill at this moment - the first time all session that has been true. Zero equity orders in this account all session, re-checked live, so it did not execute and no order exists. It is not re-struck, and the fact that it is now fillable is precisely the reason to say so rather than to quietly let it stand: a limit that expired by its own written terms is not revived by the tape finally reaching it, and re-striking a spec because the price came to it - with the thesis still forced on item 1 and no catalyst appearing since - is an entry made on price movement alone. That is the chase this slot raised bar exists to refuse, and it is more tempting when the price is better rather than less. This is also the cleanest illustration this week of why an unexecuted spec is graded by the retro and not by an hourly: the same limit read as 1.60% out of the money at 10:21, 0.29% away at 14:21, and fillable at 15:22, and any of the three could have been written up as a verdict.

NO NEW ENTRY: the mandate binds the open slot by its own text and was discharged at 09:44, and the default here is no trade. Actions 0.

The graded decision is the refusal to contract the time stop by NINE MINUTES, which is the hardest version of the refusal because it is the cheapest - and the entry says so itself rather than hiding it, that the substitution has almost no cost and that its smallness is an argument for the rule being cheap to keep rather than optional to keep. It handles the dead UPST limit turning MARKETABLE - ask 30.52 below the 30.59 limit - by reporting it precisely and refusing to revive it, on the ground that a limit expired by its own terms is not restored by the tape reaching it, and it notes that the temptation is greater when the price is better. entries.head: The time stop fires on OKLO: sell 2 at 44.70. The level was written on 8/10 and it is the calendar closing this, not the six red hours
entries.body:
THE DECISION IS THE ONE THING THIS SLOT EXISTS FOR AND IT IS AN EXIT. The 8/10 10:39 fill carried a ~5 session time stop per docs/RULES.md, struck as the 8/14 close. Today is session 5 of 5. The open wrote that level down before the session had an opinion about it, six hourly runs re-read it without contracting it, and the 15:21 hourly handed the action here explicitly: unless 54.18 or 41.54 prints first, the pre-close sells 2 shares at the bid. Neither printed. So the specification below is not a new judgement - it is the discharge of one made four sessions ago, and the only work left to this run was to check that the two price levels had not pre-empted it and to quote the exit live.

NEITHER PRICE LEVEL WAS HIT, AND SAYING SO PRECISELY MATTERS FOR THE RETRO. Against a 44.70 bid struck 19:35:35 UTC, the 54.18 target needs a further 21.21% and the 41.54 stop needs a further 7.03% down. This position is being closed by the CALENDAR, not by the tape, and the distinction is the whole content of the trade: a stop-out is the market taking a position away and a time stop is the book admitting the thesis did not happen. The record should read the second, because the second is what occurred.

WHAT THE SIX RED HOURS ARE AND ARE NOT EVIDENCE OF. 46.57 at 10:22, 45.96, 45.77, 45.29, 44.93, 44.58 at 15:21, 44.70 now - the position ran +3.15% and finished -1.00%, giving back 1.87 of bid across the session and -3.77% against the 46.45 close. Every hourly today refused to sell on that drift, on the correct ground that a trend on a chart is not a level and that 'the day will end' licenses selling at any hour. That refusal is not retroactively vindicated by the time stop arriving on schedule, and this run does not get to bank the drift as its reason now. The drift is evidence about the THESIS - six hours one direction on the final session says the move did not come - and the rulebook's instrument for a thesis that did not happen is precisely the time stop, which was already firing today regardless. The two facts agree, and only one of them is the rule.

THE ONE ARGUMENT FOR HOLDING, TAKEN SERIOUSLY AND REFUSED. It is a Friday, the position is only -1.00%, and a weekend hold costs nothing in theta on common stock. The 2026-08-10 rule answers it in one line: the ~5 session time stop is not extendable by conviction. Holding here would extend a written level because the loss is small - which is the same defect as widening a stop, pointed at the clock instead of the price, and it would convert a decision into an accident that happened to be cheap. A hold on Monday would then need its own reason, and the only one available would be that the position is still open, which is not a reason. Flat into the weekend is the decision.

EARNINGS AND THE NO-FLY WINDOW, BOTH CHECKED LIVE RATHER THAN CARRIED. The option position list was queried and is EMPTY, so no contract exists for a print to land inside and no no-fly window closes today. The earnings calendar was re-pulled across 8/14 to 8/20 and OKLO is not in it, nor is any other watched name - so nothing is dated into the weekend. No straddle was owed: the rule requiring one governs a HOLD through a print, and this run is not holding through anything.

HOW TO READ THE THREE PRICES BELOW, WRITTEN OUT BECAUSE THIS IS THE FIRST SELL SPECIFICATION THIS BOARD HAS PUBLISHED AND THE FIELDS MEAN SOMETHING DIFFERENT ON AN EXIT. The limit 44.70 is the bid, marketable and inside the 44.70/44.77 quote. The target 44.60 is the FLOOR rather than an ambition - if the bid slips in the closing minutes, complete the exit down to there rather than carry the position overnight over pennies. If OKLO gaps up Monday, this exit was still correct and the retro should not grade it as a miss: the position was given its five sessions and did not move, and a rule that is abandoned the first time it costs something was never a rule. The reading that WOULD indict it is the opposite one - if the five-session window is systematically too short for the setups this book buys, that is a finding about the rulebook to be made across the sample and by the operator, not by a run on a Friday afternoon with one position in front of it.

entries.body:
THIS ENTRY IS FORCED AND IT IS FORCED TWICE, WHICH IS WORSE THAN THE LAST FOUR AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH. Items 1 and 5 fail. The mandate requires a specification every trading day and this is the best of a poor set, not a good entry, and the difference is the whole content of this note.

WHAT IS BOUGHT. 7 SMCI at a 38.24 limit, inside a 38.21/38.25 quote struck 13:45:27 UTC. Target 45.89 (+20%), stop 35.18 (-8%), time stop the 8/21 close counting today as session 1. Cost 267.68, which is 26.5% of a 1009.16 account: the natural quarter-weight at a four-position ceiling rather than the 40% single-name maximum, because a thesis this compromised does not earn the top of its range. The stop risks 21.42, or 2.1% of the account; the target pays 53.55, or 5.3%.

ITEM 1 FAILS ON THE WHOLE BOARD, FOR A FOURTH CONSECUTIVE SESSION. The earnings calendar was pulled live across 8/17 to 8/23 and not one of the twelve watched names appears in it. SMCI reported 8/11 after the close - four sessions back - so there is no dated event inside a five-session hold on this name or on any other. The catalyst question did not rank the field today, it floored it, and the entry went to the name whose remaining checklist can be defended.

ITEM 5 FAILS, AND MARKING IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ON THIS PAGE. The rule is written around positioning into a print, and this print is behind rather than ahead, so calling it 'na' would be defensible on the letter and dishonest on the substance. The positioning the item exists to test is exactly the live question here: SMCI is 20.9% above its 31.60 pre-print close, and the four sessions since the +19.0% reaction of 8/12 are distribution rather than consolidation. 8/13 opened 38.28, touched 42.31 and closed 39.16 on 122.8M shares, giving back the whole range. 8/14 held on 62.0M. Today opened 39.31 and broke the 38.20 low of 8/13 to 37.88, with 8.9M shares done by 09:42 against a 58.0M thirty-day average, which is roughly five times normal pace for the elapsed session. I am buying into an unwind, not after one. Reading item 5 as not-applicable to reduce the forced count from two to one is precisely the move this board should distrust in itself, so it is marked fail.

THE BOARD'S OWN WRITTEN BUY CONDITION FOR THIS NAME IS NOT MET, AND I AM BUYING ANYWAY BECAUSE THE MANDATE COMPELS AN ENTRY. On 8/14 this board wrote the condition a grader can check: 'a pullback that holds - a defence of the 38.20 low or a fade toward 37.61 on lighter volume - bought there rather than here.' Neither branch is satisfied. 38.20 did not hold; it broke to 37.88. The fade toward 37.61 is arriving on price - the 8/12 close of 37.61 is the gap base and today's low sits 0.7% above it - but on HEAVIER volume, not lighter. So the correct description of this entry is early, on a name whose objection is compressing, and not vindicated.

WHY IT IS STILL FIRST, AND WHY UPST IS NOT. Friday's board ranked UPST first and wrote its invalidation in advance: 'If the 30.20/30.32 shelf gives way and the 28.14 stop is taken inside two sessions, the reading is not bad luck - it is that a setup with no catalyst had nothing holding it up.' That condition fired this morning. UPST opened 30.35, broke to a 29.80 low and is 29.92 bid, through the 30.20 close-line, through the 30.32 pre-earnings level, and through Friday's 30.25 low. A pre-registered disqualification that triggers and is then ignored was never a disqualification. So the name that was first is out on its own terms.

That leaves the mirror-image argument for SMCI, and it is the same argument Friday used to promote UPST from third to first: a refusal whose stated reason has expired gets re-read rather than repeated. SMCI was refused six times on a NUMBER - extension above the pre-print close with no pullback - and that number has moved 6.5 points in the buyer's favour, from 27.4% to 20.9%, while the pullback the board said was missing has now run four sessions and 9.7% off the 42.31 high. Under the standing numbers-over-narrative tiebreak, the number that drove the refusal has changed, so the refusal cannot simply be restated a seventh time. What has NOT changed is that there is no catalyst and that the unwind is still in progress, which is why this is forced rather than clean.

The asymmetry that decides between the two: UPST carries a triggered disqualification and SMCI carries an unmet precondition. The first says the thesis is wrong; the second says not yet. Given an entry is compulsory today, buying the not-yet over the already-wrong is the defensible order, and I would rather be early on a compressing objection than long a broken shelf.

THE OPTIONS FINDING CHANGES TODAY AND IT NO LONGER SAYS WHAT THIS BOARD HAS BEEN SAYING. For three sessions the refusal has been on spread, most recently 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling. That statement is FALSE of SMCI today. Four live 2026-09-18 calls, 32 days out and inside the 3-6 week rule, quote: the 40 strike 2.80/2.92 at 4.20% of mark on 14,360 open interest and 0.475 delta; the 37 strike 4.05/4.30 at 5.99% on 1,054 and 0.607 delta; the 39 strike 3.15/3.35 at 6.15% on 1,714 and 0.518 delta; the 38 strike 3.55/3.80 at 6.80% on 3,967 and 0.562 delta. Every one clears the ceiling. Every one clears delta 0.40. One contract at the 40 strike costs 286.00 at the mark against 1009.16 deployable. For the first time in this record, every mechanical option rule passes at once.

The contract is still not bought, and the honest reason is not spread. First, the 8/13 precedent, set by this board and reaffirmed on 8/14, is that the first option purchase waits for 'the next time a liquid chain appears beside a thesis that is NOT forced.' This thesis is forced twice. Abandoning a self-imposed precedent the first session it becomes inconvenient - in the direction of MORE risk on a WEAKER thesis - is the exact shape the rule-drift policy watches for, and it would be the agent loosening a rule rather than the operator. Second, arithmetic: a -40% option stop puts 114.00 at risk against the 21.42 the 7-share equity risks for the same directional view, and at 78% implied volatility the 40 strike bleeds about 0.0565 a day, roughly 0.28 or a tenth of the premium across a five-session hold, before the stock does anything. A thesis with no dated catalyst has nothing to pay for that decay. The accurate statement of the finding is now: this account's chains span roughly 4% to 23% of mark, the liquid end clears the ceiling outright and is affordable, and what stands between this board and its first option is the quality of the thesis rather than the quality of the market.

THE REST OF THE BOARD, RANKED. Third are the four green names on a 4-of-12 red tape - SMR +1.9%, MARA +1.5%, OKLO +0.3%, RGTI +0.1% - and buying the green half of a red morning is chasing green candles, which the rulebook lists by name under 'Does not fit'. SMR is additionally the name this account lost 14.0% in on 8/6. Fourth is AMD, refused by an explicit limit before any view is formed: one share at 510.63 is 50.6% of the account against the 40% single-name ceiling. Fifth are SOUN -3.5%, JOBY -0.8%, IONQ -0.2%, QBTS -0.5% and LEU -1.0%, all a week or more past their prints with no structure to put where the catalyst should be; SOUN and JOBY are weak without being at a level, which is a fact about the tape and not a setup. No limit was placed far below the market to manufacture a prettier entry, because a spec priced where it cannot fill inside 43 minutes is standing aside wearing the mandate's clothes.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS WRONG, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME. The bear case is the one I just marked fail: this is day four of an unwind of print-driven positioning, it broke its reference low on heavy volume this morning, and 37.61 is the last level between the entry and the 33.94 low of 8/12 - which sits below the 35.18 stop, so a full retrace of the gap takes me out. If the 37.61 gap base gives way and the stop is taken inside two or three sessions, the reading is NOT bad luck and not the mandate's fault. It is that I bought a name in the middle of distribution because a compressing valuation number and the best liquidity on the board were the only arguments available, and neither of those is a reason for a stock to go up inside five sessions. The setup I would rather have had is this same fade arriving at 37.61 on lighter volume with a dated event in the window, and no such thing exists on this board today.
